    "quote": "",
    "summary": "Minchihr challenges Slim to leave his fort and decide the battle by single combat; Slim accepts, fights, and is killed and beheaded by Minchihr. Slim’s forces rout, and leading warriors seek Minchihr’s protection; by their influence the forces of Slim and Tr unite under him, and he assigns rank by merit. Minchihr then pays respects to Feridn, showing deep deference. As Feridn nears death, he entrusts Minchihr to Sm and Narmn, seats Minchihr on the throne, places the crown on his head, and gives wise counsel. After Feridn’s death, Minchihr succeeds to the empire, keeps his great-grandfather’s laws, commands worship of God, and receives the people’s loyal praise and prayers.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "summarized"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "Minchihr sends Slim a message proposing that the battle be decided between the two of them, asking Slim to quit the fort and meet him so it can be seen to whom God gives victory.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "Slim descends from the fort, fights Minchihr, and is slain; Minchihr's sword severs Slim's head from his body.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "After Slim is killed, the enemy troops are defeated and flee in every direction.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "Leading warriors of the routed army seek protection from Minchihr; he grants it, and by their influence the forces of Slim and Tr unite under him; he assigns each rank according to merit.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "Minchihr visits Feridn after the victory; Feridn receives him with praises, thanksgivings, and customary honors; Minchihr dismounts and kisses the ground when he sees Feridn; they sit in the palace and congratulate themselves on success.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "As Feridn nears death, he recommends Minchihr to the care of Sm and Narmn and places Minchihr under their protection.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "Feridn directs Minchihr to be seated on the throne, puts the crown upon his head, and gives good and wise counsel.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:8",
      "text": "Upon Feridn’s death, Minchihr succeeds to the government of the empire, observes Feridn’s laws and regulations, commands worship of God, and is praised by the army and people for happiness and long life; they declare love and loyalty.",

The Sīmurgh/griffin, seeking food for its young, finds the crying child but does not devour him; instead it carries him to its mountain dwelling and raises him. A non-earthly voice tells the Sīmurgh that the child is entrusted to it under divine protection and prophesies that from him will spring a world champion who will bring honor and lasting fame. The Sīmurgh’s young are also affectionate to the child during the years of fostering.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Sm, a warrior, {
  "record_id": "batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l2929-l3036",
  "source_text_path": "texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md",
  "passage_locator": {
    "label": "MINCHIHR / ZL, THE SON OF SM / THE DREAM OF SM / RDBEH; lines 2929-3036",
    "start": "2929",
    "end": "3036",
    "translation": "Persian Literature, Volume 1",
    "notes": "Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."
  },
  "canonical_text": {
    "quote": "",
    "summary": "Sindokht averts Mihrb's plan to kill his wife and daughter by going with lavish gifts to Sam to secure Zal and Rudabeh's marriage. Sam and later King Minuchihr consent after consulting astrologers who prophesy a matchless heroic offspring. Rudabeh suffers a dangerous pregnancy; Zal burns the Simurgh's feather, summoning the Simurgh, who reassures them and gives instructions that save Rudabeh. Rustam is born extraordinarily large and fast-growing, needing the milk of ten nurses; festivities and charity follow. Grandfathers Sam and Mihrb come to see Rustam, who is presented with crown-like splendor and declares his desire for warlike deeds. Mihrb boasts of restoring Zahhak's laws; Sam prays Rustam will not become a tyrant but do good humbly before God.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "summarized"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "Mihrb considers killing his wife and daughter to avert threatened ruin, but Sindokht proposes visiting Sam to support her plan for Zal and Rudabeh's marriage, and Mihrb agrees.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "Sindokht travels to Zabul with extensive gifts (money, horses, attendants with trays of valuables, camels, swords, crown and throne, elephants) to influence Sam.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "Sam accepts the gifts and supports the union despite fearing Minuchihr's anger and Zal's despair.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "Minuchihr reads Sam's letter, accepts pacific proposals favoring Mihrb and the marriage, and astrologers predict the couple's child will be a hero of unmatched strength and valor.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "Zal and Rudabeh marry at a summer-house where they first met; Sam attends in Kabul and later returns to Sistan for war preparations.",
      "category": "setting",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "Near childbirth Rudabeh becomes dangerously ill; Zal uses a Simurgh feather by placing it on fire, causing darkness and the Simurgh's sudden appearance.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "The Simurgh asks why there is grief, foretells the birth of a mighty child who will be a wonder, and gives advice that is followed so that Rudabeh is soon out of danger.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4", "ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:8",
      "text": "Rustam is born prodigiously large; on the first day he looks a year old and requires the milk of ten nurses; later he eats like a man at five and is very powerful by eight.",
      "category": "attribute",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5", "ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:9",
      "text": "A silk likeness of Rustam as a mounted, armed warrior is sent to Sam in battle, bringing him great joy; widespread feasting and charity follow the news.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:10",
      "text": "Mihrb and Sam travel to see Rustam; Rustam is mounted on an elephant and wears a splendid crown during the reception arrangements.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:11",
      "text": "Rustam tells Sam he has no taste for leisure or music and longs to meet foes while mounted and armed, bringing severed heads before Sam.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:12",
      "text": "During a royal feast, Mihrb boasts that aided by Rustam's sword and mace he will restore Zahhak's laws; Sam prays to Heaven that Rustam will not become a tyrant but will do good and be humble before God.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:9"]
    }
  ],
  "figures": [
    {
      "id": "fig:1",
      "name_or_label": "Mihrb",
      "description": "A ruler/father figure who fears desolation, accepts Sindokht's plan, later boasts at a feast about being protected by Rustam and restoring Zahhak's laws.",
      "role_refs": ["role:3", "role:9"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:9"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:2",
      "name_or_label": "Sindokht",
      "description": "A woman who devises a plan to visit Sam with lavish gifts to secure Zal and Rudabeh's marriage and is distressed during Rudabeh's dangerous pregnancy.",
      "role_refs": ["role:1", "role:7"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:3",
      "name_or_label": "Sam",
      "description": "A powerful elder warrior who accepts gifts, supports the marriage, fights in Mazanderan, rejoices at Rustam's birth, hosts a royal feast, and prays Rustam will not be a tyrant.",
      "role_refs": ["role:2", "role:6", "role:8"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:6", "ev:9"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:4",
      "name_or_label": "Zal",
      "description": "Son of Sam; lover and husband of Rudabeh; uses the Simurgh's feather on fire to summon the Simurgh and follows its instructions.",
      "role_refs": ["role:4", "role:6"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2", "ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:5",
      "name_or_label": "Rudabeh",
      "description": "Bride of Zal; suffers extreme illness in pregnancy and later safely gives birth to Rustam after following the Simurgh's advice.",
      "role_refs": ["role:5"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3", "ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:6",
      "name_or_label": "Minuchihr",
      "description": "A king who consents to the marriage after reading Sam's letter and consulting astrologers.",
      "role_refs": ["role:10"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:7",
      "name_or_label": "Astrologers (of Minuchihr)",
      "description": "Advisers who prophesy that Zal and Rudabeh's offspring will be a hero of matchless strength and valor.",
      "role_refs": ["role:11"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:8",
      "name_or_label": "The Simurgh",
      "description": "A powerful being summoned by burning a feather; speaks, prophesies a mighty child, and gives instructions that save Rudabeh.",
      "role_refs": ["role:12", "role:11"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4", "ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:9",
      "name_or_label": "Rustam",
      "description": "Child of Zal and Rudabeh, born extraordinarily large and fast-growing; presented in royal splendor and speaks of his desire for battle.",
      "role_refs": ["role:13", "role:14"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5", "ev:7", "ev:8"]
    }
  ],

{
  "record_id": "batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l3038-l3128",
  "source_text_path": "texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md",
  "passage_locator": {
    "label": "MINCHIHR / ZL, THE SON OF SM / THE DREAM OF SM / RDBEH; lines 3038-3128",
    "start": "3038",
    "end": "3128",
    "translation": "Persian Literature, Volume 1",
    "notes": "Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."
  },
  "canonical_text": {
    "quote": "",
    "summary": "Rustem kills Minchihr’s loose white elephant at Sistan with a single blow. Zal then proposes that Rustem avenge an ancestor’s death connected to an enchanted mountain fort. Rustem disguises himself as a salt-merchant to gain entry, attacks by night, kills the fort’s leaders and garrison, finds a temple-like treasury, takes wealth, and—on Zal’s command—removes what he can, burns and destroys the stronghold, and returns to be honored and embraced by his parents and community.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "summarized"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "Rustem goes out at night with a mace to confront a loose white elephant that is trampling people, and he kills it with one blow.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "Servants attempt to stop Rustem from going out in the dark; he knocks down a watchman who dies, breaks the gate lock, and leaves.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "Zal praises Rustem’s valor and thanks heaven after hearing Rustem killed the elephant.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "Zal recalls an earlier expedition against an enchanted fort on Mount Sipund in which Narman was killed by a rock thrown from above by the besieged; the fort is described as extremely high and containing gardens and treasure.",
      "category": "setting",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "Sam later attempts the same fort but is blocked by a trackless desert and cannot find a way in or out of the gates, eventually retreating in despair.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "Rustem agrees to the venture and disguises himself as a salt-merchant, traveling with a camel caravan and hiding arms among loads of salt.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "Because salt is precious and wanted, the fort’s gates are opened and people buy salt, exchanging clothes, gold, and silver without suspicion.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:8",
      "text": "At night Rustem leads his warriors out; the Kotwal is awakened and meets the threat; Rustem kills him with a mace as fighting spreads in the fort.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:9",
      "text": "By morning Rustem kills the chief; survivors escape, and no inhabitants are left alive within the walls.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:10",
      "text": "Rustem forces open an iron gate with a battle-axe, finds a temple-like structure with jewels and gold, and the warriors take as much treasure as they can carry.",
      "category": "object",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:11",
      "text": "Rustem writes to Zal for further commands; Zal responds approvingly and instructs him to load the camels with valuables and then burn and destroy the entire place, which Rustem carries out.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:9"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:12",
      "text": "On Rustem’s return, Zal honors him publicly; his mother kisses and embraces him, and others give blessings.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:10"]
    }
  ],
  "figures": [
    {
      "id": "fig:1",
      "name_or_label": "Rustem",
      "description": "A warrior who kills the white elephant, disguises himself as a salt-merchant to enter the fort, fights through the night, kills the fort’s leaders, takes treasure, destroys the fort, and returns to honors.",
      "role_refs": ["role:1", "role:4", "role:7"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:5", "ev:6", "ev:7", "ev:8", "ev:9", "ev:10"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:2",
      "name_or_label": "Zal (Zl)",
      "description": "Rustem’s father who praises him, proposes the vengeance expedition, and commands the removal of treasure and destruction of the captured fort.",
      "role_refs": ["role:2", "role:3"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2", "ev:3", "ev:9", "ev:10"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:3",
      "name_or_label": "Sam (Sm)",
      "description": "Associated with earlier failed attempts against the enchanted fort after the death of his father.",
      "role_refs": ["role:5"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:4",
      "name_or_label": "Narman (Narmn)",
      "description": "An ancestor killed during an earlier siege attempt against the enchanted mountain fort.",
      "role_refs": ["role:6"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3", "ev:9"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:5",
      "name_or_label": "Feridun (Feridn)",
      "description": "A ruler who previously sent Narman with a large army against the enchanted fort.",
      "role_refs": ["role:8"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:6",
      "name_or_label": "Minchihr",
      "description": "Owner of the white elephant kept at Sistan.",
      "role_refs": ["role:9"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:7",
      "name_or_label": "White elephant",
      "description": "An enormous elephant that breaks loose at night, tramples people, and is killed by Rustem.",
      "role_refs": ["role:10"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:8",
      "name_or_label": "Servants/watchmen",
      "description": "People who attempt to restrain Rustem from going out at night; one watchman is knocked down and dies.",
      "role_refs": ["role:11"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:9",
      "name_or_label": "Kotwal (fort officer/guardian)",
      "description": "A fort official awakened by the night disturbance who confronts Rustem and is killed by him.",
      "role_refs": ["role:12"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:10",
      "name_or_label": "Chief of the fort",
      "description": "A leader of the fort discovered at dawn and slain by Rustem.",
      "role_refs": ["role:13"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:11",
      "name_or_label": "Garrison and inhabitants (men, women, children)",
      "description": "People inside the fort who purchase salt by day, fight by night, and are killed or flee; none remain alive within the walls after the battle.",
      "role_refs": ["role:14"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5", "ev:6", "ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:12",
      "name_or_label": "Rustem’s mother",
      "description": "A mother who kisses and embraces Rustem on his return.",
      "role_refs": ["role:15"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:10"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:13",

{
  "record_id": "batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l3192-l3288",
  "source_text_path": "texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md",
  "passage_locator": {
    "label": "THE DREAM OF SM / RDBEH / DEATH OF MINCHIHR / NAUDER; lines 3192-3288",
    "start": "3192",
    "end": "3288",
    "translation": "Persian Literature, Volume 1",
    "notes": "Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."
  },
  "canonical_text": {
    "quote": "",
    "summary": "After Minchihr dies, Nauder becomes king but quickly rules oppressively, prompting popular discontent and talk of replacing him. Sm comes to Persia, refuses the people’s request to seize the throne, and instead mediates and counsels Nauder on just rule and the transience of worldly power, invoking exemplars like Feridun and contrasting them with Zahhak. Nauder promises reform and the kingdom reunites. Meanwhile Poshang of Turan, hearing of Minchihr’s death and Persian unrest, urges his son Afrasiyab to invade in revenge; Afrasiyab is praised, his brother Aghriras advises caution, but preparations for war proceed.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "summarized"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "Nauder succeeds Minchihr as king and soon rules oppressively, extorting money and amassing wealth, causing widespread dissatisfaction.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "To avert revolt and invasion, Nauder asks Sm (in Mazandaran/Mzindern) for help; Sm arrives in the capital and is welcomed by the people, who ask him to take sovereignty.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "Sm refuses to take the throne, stating loyalty to Minchihr and duty to serve Nauder, and he calms the chiefs and acts as mediator.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "Sm advises Nauder to remember Feridun, govern so his name is honored, and reflects that the world is not a place of rest; death can cast a monarch down; Heaven is contrasted with earthly joys; Feridun is honored while Zahhak is cursed.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "Nauder’s government changes; he promises to rule by the principles of Hushang (Hsheng), Feridun, and Minchihr, and the kingdom reunites under him.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "Poshang of Turan, learning of Minchihr’s death and Persian unrest, seeks revenge for Salm (Slim) and Tur (Tr) and calls his son Afrasiyab; a large army is gathered.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "Aghriras, Afrasiyab’s brother, urges prudence, citing Persian warriors (Sm, Krun, Garshasp) and prior war outcomes; Poshang insists vengeance is justice for a grandson and orders Aghriras to accompany Afrasiyab; preparations are completed.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    }
  ],
  "figures": [
    {
      "id": "fig:1",
      "name_or_label": "Nauder",
      "description": "Successor to Minchihr; initially oppressive but later promises reform after Sm’s counsel.",
      "role_refs": ["role:1", "role:7"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:2",
      "name_or_label": "Minchihr",
      "description": "Deceased prior king whose death triggers succession and foreign opportunism.",
      "role_refs": ["role:6"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:3",
      "name_or_label": "Sm",
      "description": "A champion summoned for assistance who refuses kingship, mediates, and counsels the king on justice and mortality.",
      "role_refs": ["role:2", "role:3"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2", "ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:4",
      "name_or_label": "People/chiefs/courtiers of Persia",
      "description": "Subjects and elites distressed by oppression; they welcome Sm and ask him to take sovereignty.",
      "role_refs": ["role:4"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:5",
      "name_or_label": "Feridun (Feridn)",
      "description": "Held up as an honored exemplar of good rule and remembrance.",
      "role_refs": ["role:6"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3", "ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:6",
      "name_or_label": "Hushang (Hsheng)",
      "description": "Named as a model whose principles Nauder promises to follow.",
      "role_refs": ["role:6"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:7",
      "name_or_label": "Zahhak (Zohk)",
      "description": "Contrasted with Feridun as a figure whose memory is cursed.",
      "role_refs": ["role:8"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:8",
      "name_or_label": "God / Heaven",
      "description": "Invoked as a moral authority: Sm says seizing the throne would be offensive in the eyes of God; Heaven is contrasted with earthly joys.",
      "role_refs": ["role:9"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2", "ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:9",
      "name_or_label": "Poshang",
      "description": "Sovereign of Turan who decides to invade and avenge kin after hearing Persian weakness.",
      "role_refs": ["role:5"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5", "ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:10",
      "name_or_label": "Afrasiyab (Afrsiyb)",
      "description": "Poshang’s heroic son; praised with comparisons (lion/elephant; shadow miles; tongue like sword; heart like ocean; hands like rain clouds) and set to lead an army.",
      "role_refs": ["role:10"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5", "ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:11",
      "name_or_label": "Aghriras (Aghrras)",
      "description": "Brother of Afrasiyab who advises prudence and warns against ruin and desolation.",
      "role_refs": ["role:11"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:12",
      "name_or_label": "Salm (Slim) and Tur (Tr)",
      "description": "Ancestors/kin whose blood Poshang claims to avenge; referenced in justification for war.",
      "role_refs": ["role:12"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5", "ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:13",
      "name_or_label": "Krun and Garshasp",
      "description": "Named Persian warriors said to still be living, cited as reasons for caution.",
      "role_refs": ["role:13"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    }
  ],
  "roles": [
    {

    {

      "assigned_to": ["fig:4"],

      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:2"]
    },
    {

      "label": "foreign aggressor king planning invasion",
      "assigned_to": ["fig:9"],
      "basis": "Poshang seizes the opportunity after Minchihr’s death and Persian unrest to plan revenge and assemble an army.",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5", "ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "role:6",
      "label": "exemplar(s) invoked for legitimate and just rule",
      "assigned_to": ["fig:2", "fig:5", "fig:6"],
      "basis": "Minchihr is the prior rightful king; Feridun and Hushang are named as models/principles for governance and honor.",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2", "ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "role:7",
      "label": "reforming ruler after admonition",
      "assigned_to": ["fig:1"],
      "basis": "Nauder promises to rule by named principles and his government changes; chiefs and captains become contented.",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "role:8",
      "label": "negative moral exemplar (cursed memory)",
      "assigned_to": ["fig:7"],
      "basis": "Zahhak is contrasted with Feridun; curses load Zahhak’s memory.",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "role:9",
      "label": "divine/moral authority in whose eyes actions are judged",
      "assigned_to": ["fig:8"],
      "basis": "Sm frames seizing the throne as offensive to God and contrasts earthly joy with Heaven.",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2", "ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "role:10",
      "label": "heroic war leader/avenger",
      "assigned_to": ["fig:10"],
      "basis": "Afrasiyab is urged to take vengeance; an army is assembled; he is praised as powerful and brave.",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5", "ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "role:11",
      "label": "cautious advisor warning against ruin",
      "assigned_to": ["fig:11"],
      "basis": "Aghriras recommends not beginning the contest and warns of ruin and desolation.",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "role:12",
      "label": "slain kin whose deaths motivate vengeance",
      "assigned_to": ["fig:12"],
      "basis": "Poshang seeks revenge for the blood of Salm and Tur; vengeance framed as a grandson’s duty.",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5", "ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "role:13",
      "label": "named defenders/warriors cited as deterrents",
      "assigned_to": ["fig:13"],
      "basis": "Sm, Krun, and Garshasp are listed as living warriors who should make Turan prudent.",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    }
  ],
  "symbols": [
    {

Afrsiyb retaliates by killing the captive Nauder. Ts and Gustahem flee to Sistan under Zāl. Zāl attempts to elevate Afrsiyb’s brother Aghrras as king of Persia, but Afrsiyb kills Aghrras. Zāl then seeks a ruler of Feridun’s line and summons Zau, descendant of Tahmasp, who comes from island refuge, is enthroned with customary showering of gold and jewels, subdues the land, and forces Afrsiyb to retreat. Zau reigns five years, dies, and is succeeded by his son Garshasp.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Afrsiyb sends Shimass and Khazervn with thirty thousand men against Kabul and Zabul.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Zāl unites with Mihrb of Kabul, raises an army in Sistan, and fights the two generals.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Khazervn wields a battle-axe and strikes Zāl’s mail; Zāl uses his father’s mace and kills Khazervn with a blow through the head.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Rustem is confined at home with smallpox at this time.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Shimass seeks revenge but retreats when Zāl closes; his squadrons flee; Zāl pursues and slays many.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"After learning of the defeat, Afrsiyb releases Nauder from fetters and immediately kills him with a deadly blow.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Ts and Gustahem withdraw from Iran to Sistan for Zāl’s protection; Krun and those supported by Nauder also join Zāl.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Zāl judges Ts and Gustahem too young for rule and says he is not of the blood of the Kais; he seeks another to oppose Afrsiyb.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Zāl sends an envoy to Aghrras (Afrsiyb’s younger brother, governor of Ra) offering resources to place him on Persia’s throne; Aghrras accepts and travels toward Sistan.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"Afrsiyb marches to arrest Aghrras; at a conference Afrsiyb accuses him of rebellion; Afrsiyb then slays Aghrras with his sword.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"Zāl vows hostility and revenge for Nauder’s death and aims to expel Afrsiyb; he seeks help from someone of the race of Feridun.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"Tahmasp (son of Slim) fled and took refuge on an island; he died there leaving a son named Zau.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:11"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"Zāl sends Krun son of Kavah to Zau with overtures; Zau comes to Persia, fights, wins a kingdom, and is seated on the throne with the customary rite of showering gold and jewels over his head.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:12"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"After Zau subdues the country, he turns against Afrsiyb; Afrsiyb retreats to his father due to loss of Persian support and inferior position.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:13"]},{"id":"obs:15","text":"Zau reigns five years, dies, and is succeeded by his son Garshasp.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:14"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Afrsiyb","description":"A ruler who sends generals to war, kills captives and his own brother, and later retreats from Zau’s forces.","role_refs":["role:1","role:8"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:5","ev:9","ev:13"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"Zāl (Zl)","description":"A After festivities, Kai-kobd recounts a dream of two white falcons from Persia crowning him; Rustem interprets this as signaling that Zal and he are investing Kai-kobd with kingship. Rustem urges immediate departure; they travel rapidly, repel enemy detachments, and Rustem kills Keln near Persia’s borders. {
  "record_id": "batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l3932-l4054",
  "source_text_path": "texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md",
  "passage_locator": {
    "label": "AFRSIYB / GARSHSP / KAI-KOBD / KAI-KS; lines 3932-4054",
    "start": "3932",
    "end": "4054",
    "translation": "Persian Literature, Volume 1",
    "notes": "Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."
  },
  "canonical_text": {
    "quote": "",
    "summary": "Kai-ks becomes king, falls into pride and constant feasting, and is enticed by a Demon disguised as a musician who praises the land of Mzindern. Kai-ks resolves to invade Mzindern despite the alarm of his warriors. They secretly send for Zl, who warns that past great kings never attempted Mzindern and that it is an enchanted land where swords and bribery are useless. Kai-ks refuses the counsel, claiming superior power and divine protection, and orders Zl and Rustem to guard the kingdom while he wages war. The army marches; authority and treasury keys are left with Mlad under restrictions. Kai-ks orders Gw to lead chosen men forward and to burn, destroy, and kill indiscriminately to eradicate the magicians’ art.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "summarized"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "Kai-ks ascends his father's throne and the world is obedient to his will, but he deviates from recommended wise customs and rules.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "Kai-ks continually feasts and drinks wine with warriors and chiefs and becomes extravagant and proud, considering himself superior to every being on earth.",
      "category": "attribute",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "A Demon disguised as a musician comes before the monarch, plays a harp, and sings praise of Mzindern, describing it as a place of perpetual spring, beauty, birdsong, streams, and damsels.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "After hearing the song, Kai-ks determines to lead an army to Mzindern and declares his reign will exceed earlier kings (Jemshd, Zohk, Kai-kobd).",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "The warriors are alarmed and think war against the Demons will bring destruction, but they do not openly oppose the king and only suggest he reconsider.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "A messenger is sent to Zl to report that the Evil One has put destructive notions into Kai-ks's mind and to urge Zl to prevent delay.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "Zl comes to court and attempts to dissuade Kai-ks, citing that past powerful kings did not dream of conquering Mzindern and that it is a land of demon-sorcerers and enchantment where swords and bribery are useless.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:8",
      "text": "Kai-ks refuses to be diverted, claims superiority in might, army, and treasure, dismisses demon-charm fears, and states that Heaven has given him protection.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:9",
      "text": "Zl ceases opposing once convinced and returns to Sstn with melancholy forebodings; the army then sets out at dawn.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:10",
      "text": "Kai-ks leaves the charge of the empire and the keys of the treasury and jewel-chamber with Mlad, instructing him not to draw a sword without the consent and assistance of Zl and Rustem.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:11",
      "text": "Within the limits of Mzindern, Kai-ks orders Gw to select two thousand brave men with battle-axes and advance rapidly toward the city, burning and destroying valuables and killing indiscriminately by the king's command.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:9"]
    }
  ],
  "figures": [
    {
      "id": "fig:1",
      "name_or_label": "Kai-ks (king)",
      "description": "A monarch who ascends his father's throne, becomes proud and resolves to invade Mzindern.",
      "role_refs": ["role:1", "role:6"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:3", "ev:6", "ev:9"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:2",
      "name_or_label": "Demon disguised as a musician",
      "description": "A Demon who appears as a musician, plays a harp, and sings in praise of Mzindern.",
      "role_refs": ["role:2", "role:3"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:3",
      "name_or_label": "Warriors and chiefs of Kai-ks",
      "description": "The king's warriors and chiefs who feast with him and later fear the proposed war but do not openly oppose him.",
      "role_refs": ["role:4"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:4",
      "name_or_label": "Zl",
      "description": "A prominent figure summoned to court who warns against invading Mzindern and later returns to Sstn.",
      "role_refs": ["role:5"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4", "ev:5", "ev:7", "ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:5",
      "name_or_label": "Rustem",
      "description": "Named alongside Zl as a guardian of the kingdom and as one whose consent is required for defensive action while the king is away.",
      "role_refs": ["role:7"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6", "ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:6",
      "name_or_label": "Messenger to Zl",
      "description": "An unnamed messenger sent to inform Zl of Kai-ks's 'wild notions' and urge quick intervention.",
      "role_refs": ["role:8"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:7",
      "name_or_label": "Mlad",
      "description": "The person left in charge of the empire with the keys of the treasury and jewel-chamber, under restrictions.",
      "role_refs": ["role:9"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:8",
      "name_or_label": "Gw",
      "description": "A commander ordered to select two thousand brave men and advance toward the city in Mzindern, burning and killing by instruction.",
      "role_refs": ["role:10"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:9"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:9",
      "name_or_label": "Demons / demon-sorcerers of Mzindern",
      "description": "Beings associated with Mzindern, described as demon-sorcerers with enchantment and magic spells.",
      "role_refs": ["role:11"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3", "ev:5", "ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:10",
      "name_or_label": "Inhabitants encountered in Gw's advance (men, women, children)",
      "description": "People slain during the advance into Mzindern as part of the king's orders.",
      "role_refs": ["role:12"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:9"]
    }

      "assigned_to": ["fig:5"],

    }
  ],

{
  "record_id": "batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l4280-l4386",
  "source_text_path": "texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md",
  "passage_locator": {
    "label": "GARSHSP / KAI-KOBD / KAI-KS / THE SEVEN LABORS OF RUSTEM; lines 4280-4386",
    "start": "4280",
    "end": "4386",
    "translation": "Persian Literature, Volume 1",
    "notes": "Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."
  },
  "canonical_text": {
    "quote": "",
    "summary": "In the Fourth Stage of Rustem’s journey, he encounters enchanted provisions and a disguised demon-sorceress whose beauty collapses into a black fiend when Rustem offers wine in the name of God; he binds and kills her. In the Fifth Stage, Rustem passes through a region of complete darkness guided by his horse, sleeps in a cornfield, mutilates a forest-keeper who challenges him, defeats and captures the local lord Ald, and compels Ald to reveal the location and defenses of the White Demon’s caves and the prison of King Ks. Rustem and Ald travel toward Mzindern, where fires and lamps are seen at midnight; Rustem binds Ald to a tree for safekeeping and sleeps.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "summarized"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "Rustem reaches a green place with flowing rivulets and finds a ready-roasted deer with bread and salt; when he speaks, the provisions vanish, and he then sees a tambourine and a flask of wine.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "Rustem plays the tambourine and sings about his wanderings and preferred exploits; a sorceress appears in beautiful form and sits beside him.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "Rustem offers the sorceress a cup of wine in the name of God; at the mention of the Creator, her enchanted form turns into a black fiend.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "Rustem throws his kamund to secure the demon and then cuts the demon’s body in two with his sword.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "Rustem enters a region of utter darkness where neither moon nor star is visible; he loosens the rein and allows his horse Rakush to travel unguided until the darkness disperses into a bright scene of waving corn.",
      "category": "setting",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "Rustem sleeps in the field with his shield beneath his head and his sword before him.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "A forest-keeper (described as a devil) wakes Rustem by striking a staff on the ground and accuses him of letting the horse feed on the green corn-field; Rustem silently tears off the keeper’s ears.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:8",
      "text": "The forest-keeper reports to his master Ald, describing Rustem’s appearance (tiger-skin cuirass and iron helmet) and showing the severed ears.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:9",
      "text": "Ald gathers fighting men to attack; Rustem kills Ald’s leader and many troops, then uses his kamund to dismount and capture Ald alive and binds Ald’s hands.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:10",
      "text": "Rustem demands truthful guidance to the caves of the White Demon and to where King Ks is imprisoned, offering Ald the kingdom of Mzindern as reward; Ald agrees to reveal the locations and warns about the dangerous route.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6", "ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:11",
      "text": "Ald states that the White Demon reigns between two dark and lofty mountains in two hundred immeasurably deep caves, with twelve hundred demons keeping watch by night, and names Baid and Sinja; he describes a stony desert and a prodigious stream two farsangs wide guarded by warrior-demons.",
      "category": "setting",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:12",
      "text": "At midnight Rustem hears clamor and sees blazing fires and many lamps; Ald identifies it as Mzindern where the White Demon’s chiefs are gathered; Rustem binds Ald to a tree and then sleeps.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:8"]
    }
  ],
  "figures": [
    {
      "id": "fig:1",
      "name_or_label": "Rustem",
      "description": "A champion who journeys through enchanted territory, fights demons and men, captures Ald, and seeks the location of the White Demon’s caves and King Ks’s prison.",
      "role_refs": ["role:1", "role:2"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:2", "ev:5", "ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:2",
      "name_or_label": "Rakush",
      "description": "Rustem’s horse, allowed to travel unguided through darkness and later left to graze while Rustem sleeps.",
      "role_refs": ["role:3"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3", "ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:3",
      "name_or_label": "Sorceress / enchantress (demon in disguise)",
      "description": "Appears with the charms of beauty, then becomes a black fiend at the mention of the Creator.",
      "role_refs": ["role:4"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:4",
      "name_or_label": "Forest-keeper",
      "description": "A keeper of the forest (called a devil) who wakes Rustem and complains about damage to the corn-field; is mutilated and reports to Ald.",
      "role_refs": ["role:5"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:5",
      "name_or_label": "Ald",
      "description": "Lord of the land who attacks Rustem, is captured alive, and provides information about Mzindern and the White Demon’s caves and defenses.",
      "role_refs": ["role:6", "role:7"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5", "ev:6", "ev:7", "ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:6",
      "name_or_label": "White Demon",
      "description": "A ruler whose people dwell in many deep caves between two dark mountains and whose chiefs gather in Mzindern.",
      "role_refs": ["role:8"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7", "ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:7",
      "name_or_label": "King Ks",
      "description": "A king who is described as imprisoned; Rustem seeks to learn where he is held.",
      "role_refs": ["role:9"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6", "ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:8",
      "name_or_label": "Baid and Sinja",
      "description": "Named in Ald’s description of the demonic watch associated with the White Demon’s realm.",
      "role_refs": ["role:10"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:9",
      "name_or_label": "Warrior-demons / demon guards",
      "description": "A host of warrior-demons guards the banks of a wide stream and the passage to Mzindern; twelve hundred demons keep watch by night.",
      "role_refs": ["role:11"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:10",
      "name_or_label": "Ald’s fighting men (troops)",
      "description": "Men summoned by Ald to attack Rustem; many are killed and survivors flee.",
      "role_refs": ["role:12"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    }
  ],
  "roles": [
    {
      "id": "role:1",
      "label": "questing champion",
      "assigned_to": ["fig:1"],
      "basis": "Rustem travels through stages and seeks the location of the White Demon’s caves and where King Ks is imprisoned.",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "role:2",

    "quote": "",
    "summary": "Rustem mounts his horse Rakush, confronts and beheads the demon chief Arzang, and the other demons flee. Rustem returns, frees his guide Ald, and goes to the city of Mzindern where the captive king Kai-ks hears Rakush and rejoices. Rustem is welcomed by the king and warriors, but the king and his men remain blind under demonic spells and warn Rustem to conceal Rakush from sorcerers. Rustem is instructed to assault the demons’ cavern beyond the Seven Mountains and to defeat the White Demon; a cure is described in which warm blood from the White Demon’s heart, dropped into the eyes, removes blindness. Guided by Ald, Rustem reaches the Seven Mountains, waits until the heat of the sun when most demons sleep, binds Ald to a tree, and attacks and slays the sleeping demons in a cavern before hastening toward the White Demon.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "summarized"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "At dawn Rustem rises, mounts Rakush, arms himself (helmet and tiger-skin), and goes out seeking the demon chief Arzang.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "Rustem confronts Arzang outside a tent, seizes him, tears off his head, and casts it away; the surrounding demons recoil and flee in fear.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "Afterward Rustem returns to where he left Ald, releases him, and sits under a tree while recounting his deeds.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "Rustem enters the city of Mzindern; the neighing of Rakush reaches the ears of the captive king Kai-ks, who rejoices, while others initially doubt him.",
      "category": "setting",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "Kai-ks and his warriors are described as blind under demonic influence and spells; Kai-ks warns Rustem to conceal Rakush from sorcerers to avoid provoking a demonic army.",
      "category": "attribute",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "A plan is given: Rustem must storm the demons’ cavern beyond the Seven Mountains and defeat the White Demon to restore sight to the king and warriors.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "A specific cure is stated: warm blood from the White Demon’s heart, dropped in the eye, removes blindness.",
      "category": "other",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:8",
      "text": "Guided by Ald, Rustem reaches the Haft-koh (Seven Mountains), finds many companies of demons and a crowded cavern, and learns they usually sleep when the sun is hot except a small watch.",
      "category": "setting",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:9",
      "text": "Rustem waits until the sun is high, binds Ald hand and foot to a tree with thongs from his kamund, draws his sword, and slays many prostrate demons; survivors flee in terror.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:10",
      "text": "Rustem then hastens forward to encounter the White Demon.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    }
  ],

Sudaveh warns Kaus that her father's invitation is treacherous, but Kaus visits anyway and is lavishly entertained for seven days. On the following night soldiers seize Kaus and his principal warriors, plunder his tents and treasure, and imprison them in a remote mountain fortress guarded by a thousand men. Sudaveh insists she prefers death to separation and is taken to the same dungeon. content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l4717-l4801","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md","passage_locator":{"label":"KAI-KOBD / KAI-KS / THE SEVEN LABORS OF RUSTEM / INVASION OF IRN BY AFRSIYB; lines 4717-4801","start":"4717","end":"4801","translation":"Persian Literature, Volume 1","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"News spreads that Ks has been imprisoned. Afrsiyb invades and conquers Irn. Survivors inform Rustem, who raises troops and sends a demand to the king of Hmvern to release the prisoners; the king refuses and challenges Rustem. Rustem journeys by land and water to Hmvern, fights the king’s army and allied forces from Berber and Misser, wreaks heavy slaughter, and captures the king of Misser with a kamund (noose). He then defeats the troops of the Shh of Berberistn and takes the shh and chiefs prisoner. The king of Hmvern offers to stop the fight and surrender Ks, warriors, and plundered treasure; Rustem accepts, stating he came only to free Ks.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The imprisonment of Ks becomes widely known, and Afrsiyb gathers an immense army, invades Irn from Trn, and conquers it after three months, spreading ruin and desolation.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Escapees go toward Zbulistn and inform Rustem about Ks’s misfortunes; Rustem deems it necessary to liberate his sovereign and assembles troops.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Rustem sends a messenger to Hmvern with a letter demanding release of the prisoners and threatens the king with the fate of the White Demon and the magician-monarch of Mzindern if he refuses.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The king of Hmvern replies defiantly that Rustem may come and be placed in the same situation as Ks.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Rustem leaves Zbulistn and after an arduous journey by land and water arrives at the confines of Hmvern.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"A battle occurs; the king of Hmvern’s troops flee, and he solicits help from the chiefs of Berber and Misser, resulting in three kings’ armies opposing Rustem.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Rustem expresses confidence, saying that numbers do not matter when Heaven is on his side.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Rustem orders trumpets to sound, charges mounted on Rakush, and commits dreadful havoc with his falchion.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"The king of Misser advances but flees after receiving a hard blow; Rustem pursues, catches him with a kamund (noose) around his loins, drags him from his horse, and delivers him to Bhrm, who binds him.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"Rustem proceeds against the troops under the Shh of Berberistn, aided by Zra, and makes the shh and forty principal chiefs prisoners of war.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"The king of Hmvern sends a messenger asking for suspension of the fight and offers to deliver up Ks, his warriors, and plundered regal property and treasure; troops of the three kingdoms ask for quarter, and Rustem Sohrb insists fate cannot be resisted, declares ambitions to overthrow the Persian king (Ks), unite Iran and Turan under his hand, and seeks a prince-worthy horse. After searching many steeds, he is given the ‘destined’ steed bred from Rakush and prepares for war; his fame draws thousands, and his grandsire supplies treasure.   "canonical_text": {
    "quote": "",
    "summary": "At night in a war-camp, Rustem receives the king’s assent to reconnoiter the enemy and goes in Turkish disguise to observe Sohrab’s banquet. Tahmineh has earlier charged Zinda-ruzm to guard Sohrab and, if danger arises, to present the child before his father’s eyes. Zinda-ruzm notices the concealed watcher and challenges him, but is struck down and dies unseen. Sohrab discovers Zinda-ruzm’s body by torchlight, mourns and vows revenge, then orders the feast to continue. Later Gw, serving as sentinel, meets Rustem, who reports Sohrab’s stature and Zinda-ruzm’s death to the monarch. At dawn Sohrab arms himself and interrogates the captive Hujr for information about the opposing leaders; Hujr agrees to speak truthfully and begins by identifying the king’s central pavilion, described with banners, a sapphire throne, and elephants bound around it.",

  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "A chief asks the king for the task of watching the foe at night; the king agrees and calls him a favorite of heaven and inspired by divine power.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "The champion disguises himself in Turkish clothing and secretly approaches near a palace gate to observe how chiefs are arranged.",

      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "Tahmineh gives her 'only joy' (Sohrab) to Zinda-ruzm for protection and instructs that if danger arises, the child should be presented before his father's eyes.",

      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "Zinda-ruzm sits at Sohrab’s right during an imperial banquet; many chiefs surround the throne and chant Sohrab’s renown.",

      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "Zinda-ruzm notices the concealed watcher, challenges him as a spy, and is immediately felled to the earth and dies.",

      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },

      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "Sohrab realizes Zinda-ruzm is missing, runs to the spot, and finds him dead in blood; torches display the body.",

      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "Sohrab vows revenge and threatens to bedew the land with Persian blood, then resumes the feast and orders the wine-cup to flow.",

      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {

      "text": "Gw serves as sentinel at night, confronts an approaching warrior, then learns Rustem’s 'secret tale'; Rustem later reports to the monarch about Sohrab’s stature and Zinda-ruzm’s death.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:9",
      "text": "At sunrise Sohrab arms himself with mail, a regal helm, and a bent cord described as ring within ring; he mounts or stands by a dappled steed.",

      "evidence_refs": ["ev:9"]
    },

      "text": "Sohrab questions the captive chief Hujr, promising honors and wealth for truthful answers and threatening death for noncompliance; Hujr agrees to speak truth.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:10"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:11",
      "text": "Hujr describes a central royal area with bright tapestries, a triumphal throne shining with sapphire rays, banners with golden suns, and a hundred elephants bound around the tent where King Ks holds state.",

      "evidence_refs": ["ev:11"]

{
  "record_id": "batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l6481-l6592",
  "source_text_path": "texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md",
  "passage_locator": {
    "label": "THE SEVEN LABORS OF RUSTEM / INVASION OF IRN BY AFRSIYB / THE RETURN OF KAI-KS / STORY OF SOHRB; lines 6481-6592",
    "start": "6481",
    "end": "6592",
    "translation": "Persian Literature, Volume 1",
    "notes": "Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."
  },
  "canonical_text": {
    "quote": "“Son and Father driven\n  To mortal strife! are these the ways of Heaven?”",
    "summary": "Rustem and the young warrior Sohrb fight in single combat with lances, swords, clubs, bows, and grappling. Rustem’s usual strength fails as fate prevents Sohrb from being harmed, and Sohrb strikes Rustem and rebukes him. The battle widens as armies clash; Sohrb attacks the Persian host until Rustem challenges him to fight only him. They agree to resume the contest the next day and retire to their tents. Sohrb boasts of his victories to Hmn and calls for wine before the next day. Gw and Rustem, anxious, report Sohrb’s power to the King, who spends the night in despair, agony, and prayer.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "quoted"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "A narrow space is prepared for single combat, and two fighters rush into battle using lances, then swords, then clubs/maces, then bows and arrows, and then grappling by each other’s girdle-band.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "Rustem attempts to hurl the youth from his steed, but the text states that Fate forbids the youth to bleed, and Rustem’s strength seems relaxed and he pauses in despair.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "Sohrb delivers a descending blow that wounds and stuns Rustem and tells him his power is gone and urges him to seek no more combat.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "The legions close and troop rushes on troop; Sohrb engages the Persian host and kills many until Rustem returns and challenges him for single combat rather than attacking the Persians.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "Rustem proposes they stop because night is coming and wrestle the next day; both heroes retire to their tents as night falls.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "Sohrb recounts the fight to Hmn, predicts that no Persian will survive the next day, and calls for wine to strengthen hearts.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "Gw and Rustem are distressed; Rustem reports Sohrb’s strength to the King and says they must meet again tomorrow and that victory or death is given by Heaven; the King passes the night in despair, agony, and prayer.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:8",
      "text": "The narrator explicitly characterizes the combatants as son and father driven to mortal strife.",
      "category": "relationship",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:8"]
    }
  ],
  "figures": [
    {
      "id": "fig:1",
      "name_or_label": "Rustem",
      "description": "A mighty champion who fights Sohrb, attempts to throw him from his horse, is stunned by Sohrb’s blow, challenges Sohrb to fight him alone, and reports anxiously to the King.",
      "role_refs": ["role:1", "role:2", "role:5"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:2", "ev:3", "ev:4", "ev:5", "ev:7", "ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:2",
      "name_or_label": "Sohrb",
      "description": "A stripling youth who fights Rustem, wounds and stuns him, attacks the Persian host fiercely, agrees to resume combat the next day, boasts to Hmn, and calls for wine before the next day’s fighting.",
      "role_refs": ["role:3", "role:4", "role:6"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:2", "ev:3", "ev:4", "ev:5", "ev:6", "ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:3",
      "name_or_label": "Hmn",
      "description": "Listener in Sohrb’s tent to whom Sohrb describes the fight and boasts of victory.",
      "role_refs": ["role:7"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:4",
      "name_or_label": "Gw",
      "description": "A valiant figure who stands with Rustem, is saddened by the day’s death and blood, and is associated with desponding thoughts that oppress Rustem.",
      "role_refs": ["role:8"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:5",
      "name_or_label": "The King / Monarch",
      "description": "A monarch whom Rustem seeks and reports to; he is overwhelmed in despair and passes the night in agony and prayer.",
      "role_refs": ["role:9"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4", "ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:6",
      "name_or_label": "Persian host / Persians",
      "description": "A collective force attacked by Sohrb during the wider battle and referenced as those Sohrb intends to destroy.",
      "role_refs": ["role:10"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4", "ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:7",
      "name_or_label": "Turanian/Turanian troops (spelled “Trnians” in passage)",

    }

Eventually, worn out by anguish, she dies and is described as joining her child in Heaven.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"A woman is choked by strong emotion and appears close to death until “fluttering life returned,” while matrons gather around her mourning.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"She recognizes and kisses the hoofs of a favored steed and wets them with tears.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"She repeatedly kisses Sohrab’s mail and embraces his martial robes, holding them to her breast “like an infant.”","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Reins and trappings, club, spear, sword, and shield associated with the “Stripling” are brought, and she embraces them in remembrance.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"She beats her face, clings to the items, and persists in grief day after day and night after night, refusing relief.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"At last, worn out by earthly anguish, the mother’s spirit is said to join her child in Heaven.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Grieving mother","description":"A mother who mourns intensely, embraces Sohrab’s horse and equipment, and eventually dies.","role_refs":["role:1"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:2","ev:3","ev:4"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"Sohrab (the child/stripling)","description":"The mother’s child, identified by name; his battle gear is present; he is in Heaven by the end of the passage.","role_refs":["role:2"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:3","ev:4"]},{"id":"fig:3","name_or_label":"Trembling matrons (attendants)","description":"Matrons who hasten around the woman and mourn with piercing cries.","role_refs":["role:3"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"fig:4","name_or_label":"Favourite steed","description":"A favored horse that the mother kisses and bathes with tears.","role_refs":["role:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2"]}],"roles":[{"id":"role:1","label":"mourning mother","assigned_to":["fig:1"],"basis":"She grieves for her “darling boy,” clings to his possessions, and mourns continuously until death.","evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:3","ev:4"]},{"id":"role:2","label":"deceased child/warrior","assigned_to":["fig:2"],"basis":"His mail and weapons are presented as relics of his fighting, and the mother’s spirit is said to join him in Heaven.","evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:3","ev:4"]},{"id":"role:3","label":"mourning attendants","assigned_to":["fig:3"],"basis":"They gather around her and mourn with piercing cries.","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"role:4","label":"hero’s steed (mourning object)","assigned_to":["fig:4"],"basis":"The mother gazes on the favorite steed, kisses its hoofs, and weeps over it.","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]}],"symbols":[{"id":"sym:1","label":"Hero’s steed as focus of mourning","literal_form":"The favourite steed; On a later visit she contrives to be alone with him and declares her love, urging him to accept her even after the king’s death. Saiwush refuses, fearing treachery and disloyalty to his father, but offers instead to marry Sdveh’s daughter; the king is pleased and opens his treasury. Sdveh persists, uses incantations, and later threatens Saiwush with death if he will not yield; he again refuses.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Sdveh approaches the king and proposes that his son Saiwush be married to a damsel of royal lineage, asking that he be sent to the women’s quarters to choose.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Saiwush suspects artifice, hesitates, but is sent by the king to the shubistan (women’s apartments), described as a sacred precinct with great richness and magnificence.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Sdveh is described seated on a splendid throne with a coronet and flowing hair; she descends, embraces Saiwush, and kisses his eyes and face; Saiwush withdraws and mixes among the other damsels.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Saiwush reports favorably to the king about the splendid retirement; the king urges him to choose a wife, citing astrologers’ prophecy that his marriage will bring the birth of a prince.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"On a later visit, the damsels disappear, leaving Saiwush alone with Sdveh; she speaks to him in verse praising his beauty and urging him to reveal himself; Saiwush remains silent, recalling prior treachery connected to Sdveh’s family and fearing danger.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Sdveh discards modesty, urges Saiwush to clasp her, kisses him, and proposes that when the king is dead Saiwush should take her to himself; Saiwush internally rejects the temptation as demonic and disloyal to his father while trying not to provoke her.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Saiwush says he is willing to marry Sdveh’s daughter and no other; when Sdveh conveys this to the king, the king is pleased and opens his treasury for the occasion.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Sdveh continues her designs, recites incantations to prevent disappointment or to punish Saiwush if she fails; she later threatens that he will die if he refuses her; Saiwush refuses again.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Sdveh","description":"A woman in the harem who proposes a marriage arrangement, attempts to seduce {
  "record_id": "batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l7766-l7874",
  "source_text_path": "texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md",
  "passage_locator": {
    "label": "INVASION OF IRN BY AFRSIYB / THE RETURN OF KAI-KS / STORY OF SOHRB / THE STORY OF SAIWUSH; lines 7766-7874",
    "start": "7766",
    "end": "7874",
    "translation": "Persian Literature, Volume 1",
    "notes": "Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."
  },
  "canonical_text": {
    "quote": "",
    "summary": "A son, Kai-khosru, is born to Ferangs. Prn hides the child with peasants on the mountain Kaln to prevent Afrsiyb from taking him. Afrsiyb learns of the birth through a dream and confronts Prn, who claims to have abandoned the child. Kai-khosru grows up showing royal qualities. Prn deceives Afrsiyb by presenting Kai-khosru as insane; Afrsiyb is reassured and sends him away with gifts to his mother. The people curse Afrsiyb; the city built by Saiwush has been destroyed, and animals and reptiles inhabit the site. Mother and son visit where Saiwush was killed; a tree said to have grown from blood-enriched soil is found flourishing with marvelous virtues. Elsewhere, Kai-ks and his warriors mourn Saiwush; Rustem blames Sdveh's influence for the catastrophe and kills her as punishment.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "summarized"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "A child is born to Ferangs; the child is a son named Kai-khosru.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "Prn hides Kai-khosru with peasants on the mountain Kaln to prevent Afrsiyb from taking him.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "Afrsiyb has a dream informing him of Kai-khosru's birth and summons Prn for disobedience.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "Prn tells Afrsiyb he cast away the child in the wilderness and rebukes him for unjustly killing the father and possibly the son.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "Kai-khosru grows up among peasants, excels in manly exercises, and hunts ferocious animals.",
      "category": "attribute",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "Prn tells Afrsiyb the boy found and raised by a peasant is 'little better than an idiot,' and instructs Kai-khosru to appear insane.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "Kai-khosru appears before Afrsiyb wearing a golden crown and royal girdle and answers questions in a wild, incoherent manner; Afrsiyb then lets him go to his mother with presents.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:8",
      "text": "The city built by Saiwush has been razed, and wild animals and reptiles occupy the place.",
      "category": "setting",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:9",
      "text": "At the place where Saiwush was killed, a tree said to have grown from soil enriched by his blood is found verdant and said to retain marvelous virtues.",
      "category": "object",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:10",
      "text": "Kai-ks, warriors, and Rustem mourn Saiwush; Rustem blames Sdveh's influence and kills Sdveh with his sword as punishment.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    }
  ],
  "figures": [
    {
      "id": "fig:1",
      "name_or_label": "Prn",
      "description": "An older man who protects Kai-khosru by hiding him, deceives Afrsiyb about the boy, and later reunites the youth with his mother.",
      "role_refs": ["role:1", "role:2"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:2",
      "name_or_label": "Afrsiyb",
      "description": "A king/tyrant who learns of Kai-khosru's birth through a dream, questions Prn, and is deceived into thinking the youth is deranged; later shown as remorseful and associated with the murder of Saiwush.",
      "role_refs": ["role:3"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:3", "ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:3",

      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:4",
      "name_or_label": "Kai-khosru",
      "description": "Son of Ferangs; hidden on a mountain and raised by peasants; trained in warrior arts; later feigns insanity before Afrsiyb while wearing royal insignia and is sent to his mother.",
      "role_refs": ["role:5", "role:6"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:2", "ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:5",
