content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l7876-l7975","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md","passage_locator":{"label":"INVASION OF IRN BY AFRSIYB / THE RETURN OF KAI-KS / STORY OF SOHRB / THE STORY OF SAIWUSH; lines 7876-7975","start":"7876","end":"7975","translation":"Persian Literature, Volume 1","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"A Persian champion advances against Afrsiyb. Fermurz captures Afrsiyb’s son Sarkh, who is executed; his blood is collected and his head displayed. Afrsiyb gathers his army and battle follows, including a single-combat sequence involving Plsam, Gw, Fermurz, and Rustem, culminating in Rustem humiliating Plsam and challenging Afrsiyb, who is saved by Hmn and flees. The enemy retreats toward Chinese Tartary, partly to secure Kai-khosru, while the invader rules Trn harshly for years and the realm is devastated and plundered. Rustem’s companions urge return to Persia due to the neglect of Kai-ks; Rustem departs, taking great treasure and distributing portions to Zbul/Sstn and the Persian king.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Fermurz captures Sarkh (son of Afrsiyb) during fighting after the Persian army advances into Trn.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Rustem orders Sarkh delivered to Ts for execution in the same manner as Saiwush; Sarkh pleads friendship with Saiwush but is killed; his blood is received in a dish and sent to Ks, and his severed head is suspended over the gates of the king’s palace.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Afrsiyb, hearing of his son’s death, gathers the Trnian army to resist; the armies’ movement is described as so vast that sun, moon, and stars are not visible, with noise of troops and drums and gleams of armor.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Plsam seeks to fight Rustem in single combat after Afrsiyb promises him his daughter and half the kingdom; Prn advises Plsam is too young, but Plsam proceeds.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Gw first accepts Plsam’s challenge; Fermurz intervenes, shattering Plsam’s javelin; Plsam and Fermurz fight until nearly exhausted; Rustem then confronts Plsam, who strikes Rustem’s head with such force that the sword breaks but Rustem’s hair is not disordered.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Rustem unhorses Plsam by fixing a javelin in his girdle band, drags him toward Afrsiyb, and taunts Afrsiyb about his treachery and cruelty to Saiwush; Afrsiyb then appears in arms, is unhorsed when Rustem’s javelin strikes the head of his horse, but Hmn rushes between and saves him, and Afrsiyb flees on another horse.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Rustem pursues Hmn and the fleeing Trnian troops for many farsangs; the next morning he resumes pursuit; the enemy retreats into Chinese Tartary to secure, among other advantages, the person of Kai-khosru.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The invader mounts the throne in Trn and rules about seven years with memorable severity, proscribing and putting to death anyone who mentions Afrsiyb’s name.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Ts and Gdarz receive splendid presents; Zra burns and destroys in revenge for the outrage against Saiwush; the realm is delivered over to plunder and devastation and soldiers enrich themselves with public and private wealth.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"Rustem’s companions urge return to Persia, citing the neglect suffered by Kai-ks; Rustem abandons the kingdom and the warriors take immense property in jewels and gold, part taken to Zbul and Sstn and a portion to the king of kings in Persia.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Rustem","description":"Persian champion who pursues vengeance, directs Sarkh’s execution, fights Plsam, confronts Afrsiyb, pursues the fleeing enemy, and later abandons Trn carrying off treasure.","role_refs":["role:1","role:7"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:3","ev:4","ev:5","ev:7"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"Afrsiyb","description":"King/leader of the Trnians whose son is killed; gathers his army, promises rewards for subduing Rustem, fights Rustem briefly, and is rescued by Hmn before fleeing.","role_refs":["role:2"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:3","ev:4"]},{"id":"fig:3","name_or_label":"Fermurz","description":"Warrior who captures Sarkh and later shatters Plsam’s javelin and fights him fiercely.","role_refs":["role:3"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:3"]},{"id":"fig:4","name_or_label":"Sarkh (son of Afrsiyb)","description":"Captured prisoner who is executed; his blood is collected in a dish and his head displayed over palace gates.","role_refs":["role:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"fig:5","name_or_label":"Ts","description":"Receives Sarkh from Rustem for execution; later receives splendid presents.","role_refs":["role:5"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:6"]},{"id":"fig:6","name_or_label":"Ks (Khosru)","description":"Recipient of Sarkh’s blood sent in a dish; later the enemy retreats to secure Kai-khosru’s person.","role_refs":["role:6"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:5"]},{"id":"fig:7","name_or_label":"Plsam","description":"Brother of Prn who seeks single combat against Rustem for promised rewards; fights Gw and Fermurz and is finally unhorsed and humiliated by Rustem.","role_refs":["role:8"],"evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:4"]},{"id":"fig:8","name_or_label":"Prn (Pirn)","description":"Brother of Plsam who cautions that Plsam is too young to match Rustem’s experience and valor.","role_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"fig:9","name_or_label":"Gw (Giv)","description":"Hears Plsam’s summons and accepts the challenge before Fermurz intervenes.","role_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"fig:10","name_or_label":"Rakush","description":"Rustem’s gallant steed, pushed forward as Rustem confronts Plsam.","role_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"fig:11","name_or_label":"Hmn","description":"Rushes between Rustem and Afrsiyb to save his master and later attempts to escape from Rustem’s pursuit.","role_refs":["role:9"],"evidence_refs":["ev:4","ev:5"]},{"id":"fig:12","name_or_label":"Gdarz","description":"Receives splendid presents suitable to his rank and services.","role_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"fig:13","name_or_label":"Zra","description":"In revenge for the outrage against Saiwush, burns and destroys everything encountered; is stirred by places where the young prince had resided.","role_refs":["role:10"],"evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"fig:14","name_or_label":"Saiwush","description":"Earlier slain figure referenced as the model for Sarkh’s execution and as the victim of Afrsiyb’s treachery and cruelty.","role_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:4","ev:6"]},{"id":"fig:15","name_or_label":"Kai-ks","description":"Figure said to have suffered neglect for many years, cited as a reason to return to Persia.","role_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:7"]}],"roles":[{"id":"role:1","label":"Persian champion and commander","assigned_to":["fig:1"],"basis":"Rustem leads actions against Afrsiyb, directs execution, fights and pursues enemies.","evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:4","ev:5"]},{"id":"role:2","label":"Turanian/Trnian king and antagonist leader","assigned_to":["fig:2"],"basis":"Afrsiyb commands the Trnian army, offers rewards, fights, and flees.","evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:4"]},{"id":"role:3","label":"Capturing warrior (Persian side)","assigned_to":["fig:3"],"basis":"Fermurz takes Sarkh prisoner and intervenes in combat by shattering a javelin.","evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:3"]},{"id":"role:4","label":"Captured prince executed as vengeance","assigned_to":["fig:4"],"basis":"Sarkh is taken prisoner and put to death; blood collected; head displayed.","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"role:5","label":"Executioner/agent delegated by Rustem","assigned_to":["fig:5"],"basis":"Rustem delivers Sarkh to Ts to be put to death; Ts later receives gifts.","evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:6"]},{"id":"role:6","label":"Recipient of a blood-token/message","assigned_to":["fig:6"],"basis":"Sarkh’s blood in a dish is sent to Ks; later Kai-khosru is a strategic objective.","evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:5"]},{"id":"role:7","label":"Occupying ruler of Trn","assigned_to":["fig:1"],"basis":"The invader mounts the throne in Trn and rules about seven years with severe proscriptions.","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"role:8","label":"Single-combat challenger seeking reward","assigned_to":["fig:7"],"basis":"Plsam challenges Rustem after Afrsiyb promises daughter and half the kingdom.","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"role:9","label":"Royal rescuer/protector","assigned_to":["fig:11"],"basis":"Hmn rushes between to save Afrsiyb and facilitates his escape.","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"role:10","label":"Avenger through devastation","assigned_to":["fig:13"],"basis":"Zra burns and destroys in revenge for the outrage committed upon Saiwush.","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]}],"symbols":[

content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l8495-l8583","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md","passage_locator":{"label":"THE RETURN OF KAI-KS / STORY OF SOHRB / THE STORY OF SAIWUSH / KAI-KHOSRU; lines 8495-8583","start":"8495","end":"8583","translation":"Persian Literature, Volume 1","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"A Persian force under Ts takes forts and fights Turanian/Tartar forces. In a fort assault, Ferd is killed by Bhrm during combat; Ferd’s mother Glshaher kills herself from grief. Ts later suffers a disastrous night attack while his troops are off-guard. Kai-khosru orders Ts arrested for disobeying instructions to avoid Kullab (where the king’s brother and mother lived) and causing their deaths. In later battles, Frburz is driven to take refuge near a mountain; Byzun kills a standard-bearer to seize the imperial banner (Derafsh Gvahn) and deliver it to Gdarz. Massive casualties follow, and victory goes to the Turanians. Afrsiyb rewards officers; Khosru mourns and seeks Rustem’s counsel. Ts is released and again sent to war; after prolonged fighting, the warrior Hmn challenges and kills several opponents in single combat, and later fights Gw to a stalemate.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Ts attacks a fort, bursts open its gates, and fighting occurs involving Ferd, Byzun, and Bhrm; Bhrm strikes Ferd on the head and kills him.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Glshaher, Ferd’s mother, embraces the dead Ferd in grief and kills herself by plunging a dagger into her breast.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Ts remains three days, erects a lofty monument to Ferd’s memory, and scents it with musk and camphor.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Prn-wsah withdraws to attempt a shubkhn (night attack); at night the Persians are off guard and many are intoxicated, and the Tartars cause heavy destruction.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Kai-khosru writes that he warned Ts not to go by the way of Kullab because the residence of the king’s brother and his mother was there and should be kept sacred; he orders Ts bound and sent as a prisoner, and Frburz to assume command.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Frburz confines Ts and sends him to Khosru; Khosru reproaches Ts and consigns him to a dungeon.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"In a later battle, the enemy turns to attack Frburz; Frburz shelters remaining troops on the skirts of a mountain; Gdarz and Gw request either Frburz’s support or the imperial banner be sent to them.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Frburz refuses to give up the imperial banner; Byzun kills the standard-bearer and takes the Derafsh Gvahn to Gdarz, who raises it and leads a charge with great carnage.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Only eight of Gdarz’s sons remain alive and many kin are slain; many of the family of Ks are killed; nine hundred relatives of Afrsiyb and Prn die; victory remains with the Turanians.","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"Afrsiyb sends presents and honorary dresses to officers and urges them to further obscure the martial glory of Rustem and Khosru; Prn replies that it will be accomplished.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"After defeat, Frburz retreats by night to Khosru’s court; Khosru mourns the loss in battle and the death of his brother Ferd; Rustem is applied to for consolation and to extricate the empire from misfortunes.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:11"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"Khosru liberates Ts from confinement; Ts and Gdarz are deputed with a large army; the two powers fight for seven days and nights; on the eighth Hmn challenges and kills several warriors in single combat; Gw fights Hmn and both withdraw; battle continues undecided.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:12","ev:13"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Ts","description":"Persian commander who attacks forts, later suffers defeat, is arrested by order of Kai-khosru, imprisoned, then later liberated and deputed again to war.","role_refs":["role:1","role:10"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:5","ev:6","ev:12"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"Ferd","description":"A youth who fights with valor against Byzun and is killed by Bhrm; identified as Kai-khosru’s brother in Khosru’s mourning.","role_refs":["role:3","role:7"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:11"]},{"id":"fig:3","name_or_label":"Byzun","description":"A warrior who fights in contests, is rescued from capture, later serves as messenger to Frburz and takes the imperial banner after killing the standard-bearer.","role_refs":["role:4","role:12"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:4","ev:7","ev:8"]},{"id":"fig:4","name_or_label":"Bhrm","description":"A hero who springs from ambush and kills Ferd by striking his head.","role_refs":["role:5"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"fig:5","name_or_label":"Glshaher","description":"Ferd’s mother who kills herself with a dagger after seeing her son dead.","role_refs":["role:2"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"fig:6","name_or_label":"Kai-khosru (Khosru)","description":"King who warns Ts, orders his binding and transfer as prisoner, reproaches him, later mourns losses, seeks Rustem’s help, liberates Ts, and deputes content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l8585-l8691","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md","passage_locator":{"label":"THE RETURN OF KAI-KS / STORY OF SOHRB / THE STORY OF SAIWUSH / KAI-KHOSRU; lines 8585-8691","start":"8585","end":"8691","translation":"Persian Literature, Volume 1","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"In a battle, Piran sends a magician to a mountain to conjure darkness, snow, and hail against the Persians, leading to their defeat. Tus and Gudarz pray to God for deliverance from sorcery. A mysterious figure from the invisible world directs Rehm to the mountain; Rehm finds the magician, disables him, and the storm and darkness vanish, after which the magician is executed. The Persians withdraw to a mountain fortress with wells and provisions and are besieged, but Khosru sends Rustem and Fariburz as reinforcements. Piran seeks additional allies from Afrasiyab, who sends prominent confederates including the Khakan of Chin and Kamus of Kushan. Battle resumes; Rustem prays and fights. Ushkabs advances against Rehm; after Rehm withdraws, Rustem approaches Ushkabs on foot with bow and arrows.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Piran sends Bar, a renowned magician, to neighboring mountains to conjure darkness and stormy snow and hail directed against the enemy while sparing the Turanian army.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"When Humn and Piran-viseh attack with the storm’s aid, the Persian army suffers a severe overthrow and heavy carnage.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Tus and Gudarz pray to God for protection and deliverance from sorcery aiding the foe.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"A mysterious person appears to Rehm from the invisible world and indicates the mountain where the tempest originates.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Rehm rides to the mountain, finds the magician on the summit performing incantations, cuts off his arms, and the darkness and hail/snow immediately dissipate; Rehm then brings the magician before Tus and kills him.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The armies pause to rest, then fight again; the Persians retreat to the mountain Hamwun and place their sick and wounded in a fortress there while Tus stays forward to protect them.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Piran orders a siege of Tus’s position; despite conflicts he gains no advantage, and the mountain fortress has wells of water and abundant grain and provisions so starvation is not a threat.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Khosru sends Rustem with Fariburz to assist; they are welcomed, the gates are opened, and Rustem is seen seated on a throne in a public hall deliberating with army leaders.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Piran-viseh reports to Afrasiyab that the Persians are confined in a mountain fort and requests reinforcements; Afrasiyab dispatches Shinkul of Sughsar, the Khakan of Chin, and Kamus of Kushan.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"Kamus is described as affecting the air and weather metaphorically by his frown and smile, and he boasts he will defeat Rustem in single combat.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:6","ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"On the next day, the armies are drawn up; Rustem prays to the Creator and enters battle amid dust that darkens earth and sky and widespread slaughter.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"Ushkabs advances from the Tartar army; Rehm fights him with difficulty and retreats; Rustem, seeing this, goes forward on foot with bow and arrows and addresses Ushkabs.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Piran (Prn)","description":"A commander who employs a magician to conjure a storm, orders a siege, and coordinates allies and battle arrangements.","role_refs":["role:1"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:4","ev:6","ev:7"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"Bar (Br), magician","description":"A renowned magician sent to a mountain to create darkness and snow/hail by incantations.","role_refs":["role:2"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:3"]},{"id":"fig:3","name_or_label":"Humn (Hmn)","description":"An attacker who advances in concert with Piran-viseh during the storm.","role_refs":["role:3"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"fig:4","name_or_label":"Piran-viseh (Prn-wsah)","description":"A leader who attacks with Humn and later writes to Afrasiyab requesting reinforcements.","role_refs":["role:3"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:6"]},{"id":"fig:5","name_or_label":"Tus (Ts)","description":"A Persian leader who prays to God, receives the captured magician, shelters wounded in a mountain fortress, and is besieged.","role_refs":["role:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:3","ev:4"]},{"id":"fig:6","name_or_label":"Gudarz (Gdarz)","description":"A Persian leader who joins Tus in prayer to God for deliverance from sorcery.","role_refs":["role:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"fig:7","name_or_label":"God / the Creator","description":"Addressed in prayer for protection from sorcery; Rustem also prays before entering battle.","role_refs":["role:5"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:7"]},{"id":"fig:8","name_or_label":"Mysterious person from the invisible world","description":"A figure who appears to Rehm and points out the mountain source of the tempest.","role_refs":["role:6"],"evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"fig:9","name_or_label":"Rehm","description":"A fighter who is guided to the mountain, disables the magician causing the storm to cease, later fights Ushkabs and withdraws.","role_refs":["role:7"],"evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:8"]},{"id":"fig:10","name_or_label":"Khosru","description":"A ruler who sends Rustem and Fariburz to relieve the besieged Persians.","role_refs":["role:8"],"evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"fig:11","name_or_label":"Rustem","description":"A leading warrior sent to assist; he deliberates in the fortress, prays, enters battle, and advances toward Ushkabs.","role_refs":["role:7"],"evidence_refs":["ev:5","ev:7","ev:8"]},{"id":"fig:12","name_or_label":"Fariburz (Frburz)","description":"Accompanies Rustem as reinforcement to the mountain fortress.","role_refs":["role:9"],"evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"fig:13","name_or_label":"Afrasiyab (Afrsiyb)","description":"Receives request for reinforcements and dispatches confederate leaders.","role_refs":["role:8"],"evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"fig:14","name_or_label":"Shinkul of Sughsar","description":"One of three illustrious confederates sent as reinforcement.","role_refs":["role:10"],"evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"fig:15","name_or_label":"Khakan of Chin","description":"A confederate leader whose crown is described as the starry heavens; coordinates with Piran for battle.","role_refs":["role:10"],"evidence_refs":["ev:6","ev:7"]},{"id":"fig:16","name_or_label":"Kamus of Kushan (Kms)","description":"A renowned hero ally who boasts he will defeat Rustem; described with imagery of frown/smile affecting cold and spring rain.","role_refs":["role:10"],"evidence_refs":["ev:6","ev:7"]},{"id":"fig:17","name_or_label":"Ushkabs","description":"A leader who advances from the Tartar army and fights Rehm; is then approached by Rustem.","role_refs":["role:11"],"evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"fig:18","name_or_label":"Persian army / Persian hosts","description":"Suffers defeat under the conjured storm, retreats to a mountain fortress, and resumes battle with reinforcements.","role_refs":["role:12"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:4","ev:5","ev:7"]},{"id":"fig:19","name_or_label":"Tartar/Turanian army and allies","description":"Attacks with elemental ‘co-operation,’ later besieges the mountain fortress and fields a large force against Rustem.","role_refs":["role:12"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:4","ev:7"]}],"roles":[{"id":"role:1","label":"Enemy commander employing sorcery and siege","assigned_to":["fig:1"],"basis":"Piran sends a magician to create a storm, orders a siege, and seeks reinforcements and battle arrangements.","evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:4","ev:6","ev:7"]},{"id":"role:2","label":"Weather-conjuring magician","assigned_to":["fig:2"],"basis":"Bar is sent to mountains to conjure darkness and snow/hail and is found performing incantations on the summit.","evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:3"]},{"id":"role:3","label":"Attacking leaders in the storm-assisted assault","assigned_to":["fig:3","fig:4"],"basis":"Humn and Piran-viseh attack when the conjured elements cooperate, causing Persian defeat.","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"role:4","label":"Besieged Persian commanders and petitioners","assigned_to":["fig:5","fig:6"],"basis":"Tus and Gudarz pray for protection; Rustem prays to the Creator before battle.","evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:7"]},{"id":"role:6","label":"Supernatural messenger/guide","assigned_to":["fig:8"],"basis":"A mysterious person from the invisible world appears and points out the mountain source of the tempest.","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"role:7","label":"Warrior who counters sorcery / battlefield champion","assigned_to":["fig:9","fig:11"],"basis":"Rehm locates and disables the magician, ending the storm; Rustem leads fighting and advances toward Ushkabs.","evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:7","ev:8"]},{"id":"role:8","label":"Ruler who dispatches aid or reinforcements","assigned_to":["fig:10","fig:13"],"basis":"Khosru sends Rustem and Fariburz; Afrasiyab sends confederate leaders after receiving Piran-viseh’s letter.","evidence_refs":["ev:5","ev:6"]},{"id":"role:9","label":"Reinforcement companion","assigned_to":["fig:12"],"basis":"Fariburz accompanies Rustem to assist the besieged Persians.","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"role:10","label":"Confederate allied war-leaders","assigned_to":["fig:14","fig:15","fig:16"],"basis":"Afrasiyab dispatches Shinkul, the Khakan of Chin, and Kamus of Kushan as reinforcements; content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l8810-l8919","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md","passage_locator":{"label":"THE RETURN OF KAI-KS / STORY OF SOHRB / THE STORY OF SAIWUSH / KAI-KHOSRU; lines 8810-8919","start":"8810","end":"8919","translation":"Persian Literature, Volume 1","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"Prn obtains the Khakn’s permission to negotiate with Rustem. Rustem identifies himself as armed for battle and brings blessings from Kai-khosru and his mother Ferangs, whom Prn says he protected when Afrsiyb sought to sacrifice them. Prn urges peace, claiming the confederates are guiltless of Saiwush’s blood, but Rustem demands surrender of key perpetrators (especially Gerswaz) and large payments. The Khakn’s allies reject these terms; Shinkul challenges Rustem and is quickly defeated. A larger battle follows in which Rustem kills multiple challengers, then vows to confront the Khakn and advances toward the Khakn’s headquarters, calling out to him.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Prn goes to the Khakn and is permitted to go as an envoy to confer with Rustem about peace or war.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The Khakn speaks confidently that Rustem is flesh and blood and that his forces are numerically superior (he claims three hundred for every one).","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Prn reaches the Persian camp, identifies himself to Rustem, and Rustem states he is \"Rustem of Zbul\" and is armed for battle.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Rustem says he brings blessings from Kai-khosru and Ferangs, who see Prn’s face nightly in dreams.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Prn blesses Kai-khosru and Ferangs, praises Ferangs as Afrsiyb’s daughter, and recounts that he protected Ferangs and the newborn Kai-khosru from Afrsiyb, who would have sacrificed them; they later escaped across a boundary stream.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Prn calls for peace, saying the confederates in the war are guiltless of Saiwush’s blood.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Rustem states that no peace can be made unless the principal actors in Saiwush’s death are given up (especially Gerswaz) and vast sums of money are presented; he also says he would disdain peace except that it enables Prn to serve Kai-khosru.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The Khakn and confederates reject the peace terms as ignominious; Shinkul of Ind opposes them and is allowed to begin combat.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Shinkul summons Rustem; Rustem strikes him with a spear that penetrates his breast, unhorsing him; Shinkul flees back to tell the Khakn.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"Shinkul describes Rustem as not mortal-born and likens him to an elephant in fight and a mountain, and calls him a dragon no human can withstand alone.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"Five thousand men are assigned to Shinkul; with them he returns; Rustem is joined by companions and a general battle ensues with dust obscuring the heavens and blood covering the plain.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"Swa attacks Rustem seeking revenge; Rustem uses his battle-axe and, giving Rakush the rein, kills the attacker with a blow of his mace; Rustem also kills Kahr, another kinsman of Kms.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"Rustem vows to encounter the Khakn himself and despoil him of pomp and treasure; he selects a thousand horsemen and approaches the kulub-gah (headquarters) of the monarch of Chn; Rustem calls aloud to the Khakn.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Prn","description":"An anxious envoy who negotiates with Rustem and recounts protecting Ferangs and the infant Kai-khosru from Afrsiyb.","role_refs":["role:1","role:6"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:3"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"the Khakn (monarch of Chn/Chin)","description":"Ruler who authorizes Zbul","description":"Champion of the Persian host, armed for battle, negotiates harsh peace terms, defeats challengers, and advances toward the Khakn’s Afrsiyb seeks intelligence, consults the elder Prn-wsah, and recruits the powerful Pladwund to fight Rustem. After early clashes and a hard fight, the opponents agree to wrestle without interference. Rustem throws Pladwund violently; Pladwund feigns death and escapes. Afrsiyb’s forces lose heart; Afrsiyb flees, abandoning standards, tents, arms, and treasure. Rustem sends booty to Kai-khosru, distributes some among troops, and returns to court where he is lavishly rewarded with jewels, gold vessels with musk and aloes, garments, attendants, and livestock, then returns to Zbul with widespread acclaim.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Rustem reports his success to Kai-khosru through Frburz and receives applause, then undertakes new exploits.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Rustem attacks Kafr, king of the city of Bidd, described as a cannibal who eats human flesh (especially young beautiful women), kills him, gives the body to dogs, and plunders and razes his castle.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Rustem invades and ravages the province of Khoten, a dependency of Turan and recently the possession of Saiwush, distressing {
  "record_id": "batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l9487-l9580",
  "source_text_path": "texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md",
  "passage_locator": {
    "label": "STORY OF SOHRB / THE STORY OF SAIWUSH / KAI-KHOSRU / AKWN DW; lines 9487-9580",
    "start": "9487",
    "end": "9580",
    "translation": "Persian Literature, Volume 1",
    "notes": "Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."
  },
  "canonical_text": {
    "quote": "",
    "summary": "Piran recounts to Afrasiyab the treachery of Gurgin and argues that executing Bizhan would repeat the earlier tragedy of Siavush and reignite war between Turan and Iran. Afrasiyab refuses mercy but accepts Piran's alternative: Bizhan is chained and suspended head-down in a deep pit, sealed by an immense rock said to have been dragged from the ocean by the demon Akvan Div; Manizheh is initially sentenced likewise but is instead left destitute near the pit and forbidden aid. A fissure in the sealing rock allows Bizhan's voice to be heard and food and water to be lowered. Meanwhile Gurgin searches, returns to Iran, and lies to Giv about Bizhan being carried off by a phantom-elk (possibly the White Demon). Giv punishes Gurgin and reports to Kay Khosrow, who imprisons the traitor; astrologers declare Bizhan still alive, prompting a search expedition.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "summarized"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "Piran petitions King Afrasiyab to spare Bizhan, warning that killing him would repeat the tragedy of Siavush and bring war and devastation to Turan and Iran.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "Afrasiyab insists Bizhan must die because the offense brings him shame, but after deliberation he orders Bizhan bound in chains and hung head-down inside a deep pit so he will never see sun or moon again.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "Manizheh is sentenced to share Bizhan’s fate, but Afrasiyab changes her punishment, allowing her to dwell near the pit while forbidding anyone to go to her or supply her with food; she is stripped of garments and jewels and left barefoot and bareheaded.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "A huge rock, described as dragged from the ocean by Akvan Div and flung onto the plain of Tartary, is placed over the pit’s mouth; a fissure in the rock allows Bizhan’s voice to be heard and bread and water to be lowered to him.",
      "category": "object",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "Gurgin searches for Bizhan and finds the place where Afrasiyab’s daughter had resided deserted; he later finds Bizhan’s horse astray, secures it with his lasso, and returns to Iran.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "Giv mourns Bizhan’s absence by tearing garments and hair and throwing ashes on his head, then demands an account from Gurgin and fears Bizhan has fallen into the power of demons.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "Gurgin lies to Giv, claiming Bizhan was dragged away by a strange elk-like creature; he compares it to the Simurgh and suggests it may have been the White Demon.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:8",
      "text": "Giv does not believe Gurgin’s tale, seizes him, and beats him with two hundred strokes; later Kay Khosrow imprisons Gurgin in chains rather than executing him.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:9",
      "text": "Astrologers are consulted and declare Bizhan is still living; Kay Khosrow dispatches troops to search for him.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:9"]
    }
  ],
  "figures": [
    {
      "id": "fig:1",
      "name_or_label": "Bizhan (Byzun)",
      "description": "A youth condemned to be chained and hung head-down in a deep pit, sealed under a great rock; his voice can be heard through a fissure and food and water are lowered to him.",
      "role_refs": ["role:1"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2", "ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:2",
      "name_or_label": "Piran (Prn)",
      "description": "A counselor who pleads with the king to spare Bizhan and proposes imprisonment rather than execution.",
      "role_refs": ["role:2"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:3",
      "name_or_label": "Afrasiyab (Afrsiyb)",
      "description": "A king who insists Bizhan must die for shame, then orders severe imprisonment in a pit and issues proclamations about Manizheh’s isolation.",
      "role_refs": ["role:3"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2", "ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:4",
      "name_or_label": "Gerswaz",
      "description": "An agent ordered to bind Bizhan with chains and conduct Manizheh to the pit, stripping her of garments and jewels.",
      "role_refs": ["role:4"],

  "canonical_text": {
    "quote": "",
    "summary": "Kai-khosru uses a wondrous cup (associated with Jemshid) to reveal hidden things and sees Byzun imprisoned in a cave/pit with Manjeh nearby. He summons Rustem to help rescue Byzun. Rustem chooses to travel in disguise as a merchant with a richly laden caravan and warriors dressed as camel-drivers; Girgn is allowed to accompany them while his children are held as hostages. In enemy territory Manjeh questions Rustem (not recognizing him), and after initial denial he learns her story and the location of the pit. Rustem sends food to Byzun with his seal-ring hidden inside, enabling Byzun to recognize that Rustem has come; Byzun asks Manjeh to keep the recognition secret, while Manjeh asserts her devotion and sacrifices for him.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "summarized"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "A monarch holds up a wondrous cup described as a bright mirror that reveals what is concealed in the world, including things in ocean, stars, rock, caverns, and the seven climes.",
      "category": "object",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "In the cup’s vision, Byzun is seen in a dismal cave, and Manjeh is seen sitting sad and alone on a 'demon-stone.'",
      "category": "setting",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "Kai-khosru dispatches Gw to invite Rustem, explaining that Byzun has been captured; Rustem agrees to help.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "Rustem says he needs no army and prefers to go in disguise as a merchant; a thousand camels are laden with jewels, brocades, and merchandise, and a thousand warriors are dressed like camel-drivers.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "Girgn is released from bonds to join the party, but his children are kept in prison as hostages to ensure his conduct.",
      "category": "relationship",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "Manjeh (identified as the daughter of Afrsiyb) tells Rustem of her love for Byzun and indicates a pit where Byzun is imprisoned and bound with heavy chains; she says she supplies bread and water through a fissure in a huge stone covering the pit’s mouth.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "Rustem gives Manjeh a roasted fowl with his seal-ring enclosed to pass to Byzun; Byzun recognizes Rustem by the name engraved on the ring and asks Manjeh to keep the secret.",
      "category": "object",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:8",
      "text": "Manjeh declares she has sacrificed everything for Byzun’s love and denies the possibility of being faithless to him.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:8"]
    }
  ],

{
  "record_id": "batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l10574-l10636",
  "source_text_path": "texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md",
  "passage_locator": {
    "label": "BARZ, AND HIS CONFLICT WITH RUSTEM / SSEN AND AFRSIYB / THE EXPEDITION OF GDARZ / THE DEATH OF AFRSIYB; lines 10574-10636",
    "start": "10574",
    "end": "10636",
    "translation": "Persian Literature, Volume 1",
    "notes": "Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."
  },
  "canonical_text": {
    "quote": "",
    "summary": "Afrasiyab, pursued by Kai-khosru’s army and abandoned by his followers, flees into a cave near a mountain hermit named Hm. Hearing Afrasiyab lament, Hm recognizes him, lures him out, strikes him, binds him, and delivers him to Kai-khosru. Kai-khosru recalls the basin and dagger used in the murder of Saiwush and orders Afrasiyab and the treacherous Gerswaz executed together by decapitation. Kai-khosru then returns to Iran; Rustem goes to his own principality; Kai-ks welcomes the returning conqueror and praises him for avenging Saiwush.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "summarized"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "Afrasiyab flees through wood and desert, is pursued by Kai-khosru and his army, loses followers, and receives no protection from regions he seeks for refuge.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "Afrasiyab hides alone in a cave to remain undiscovered.",
      "category": "setting",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "Hm, described as strong and brave and living a religious life on a neighboring mountain, hears lamentation at night from below and investigates.",
      "category": "attribute",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "Hm hears a mourner speaking Turkish and concludes the voice is Afrasiyab; motivated by past suffering under Afrasiyab’s tyranny, Hm approaches to confirm.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "At dawn Hm calls at the cave mouth; Afrasiyab comes out, is recognized, struck on the forehead, felled, and bound with his hands secured behind his back.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "In fetters Afrasiyab complains and asks why he is treated so; Hm answers that Afrasiyab harmed princes of Feridun’s race, drove Hm to refuge, and that God has delivered Afrasiyab into his hands.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "Afrasiyab asks Hm to kill him rather than convey him to Kai-khosru, but Hm takes him to the Persian king.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:8",
      "text": "Kai-khosru receives the prisoner exultantly, rewards Hm, recalls a basin and dagger used in Saiwush’s murder, summons Gerswaz, and orders Afrasiyab and Gerswaz put to death together; the two are executed by decapitation.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:9",
      "text": "After the executions, Kai-khosru returns to Iran, Rustem proceeds to his principality, and Kai-ks welcomes Kai-khosru, praising him especially for avenging the murder of his father Saiwush.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    }
  ],

    },

      "role_refs": ["role:3", "role:4"],

    },

      "role_refs": ["role:8"],

    },
    {

      "role_refs": [],

    },
    {

Gushtsp (Gushtasp), feeling disfavored in succession compared with sons of Kai-khosru’s line, rebels and raises a large force to go toward Hindustan, but his brother Zarr persuades him to return on condition he be named heir. Lohursp does not favor Gushtsp’s elevation; Gushtsp leaves again alone for Rum, falls into poverty, seeks work (as scribe, then with camel-drivers), receives a meal, then works for a blacksmith and breaks an anvil with a blow, leading to his expulsion. Traveling onward, he is aided by a husbandman; they discover claimed shared ancestry (Feridun/Husheng line) and live together amicably until Gushtsp’s fortune begins to improve and Heaven’s favor is said to appear.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Lohursp is described as having a very high reputation and as administering his kingdom justly and paternally; he says he must surpass Kai-khosru in moderation and clemency to the poor.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Lohursp has four sons: Ardshr and Shydasp by the daughter of Kai-khosru (as stated), and Gushtsp and Zarr by another woman.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Gushtsp is described as intrepid and acute and seemingly marked for sovereignty, but he is not a favorite with his father due to independent conduct.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Gushtsp collects one hundred thousand horsemen and proceeds toward Hindustan of his own accord.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Lohursp sends Zarr with one thousand horsemen to influence Gushtsp to return; Zarr overtakes him and argues with him.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Gushtsp tells Zarr they lack Kainian blood to boast and therefore cannot expect the diadem or throne from Lohursp; he says they must seek other means for fortune.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Gushtsp agrees to return only on condition that he be nominated heir to the throne and treated with respect and ceremony; Zarr agrees to interpose his efforts and brings him back.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"It becomes apparent that Lohursp does not intend to elevate Gushtsp over the claims of his other sons; Gushtsp flees his father’s house alone and goes toward Rum.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Lohursp again sends Zarr to search for Gushtsp, but Zarr returns without finding him.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"In Rum, Gushtsp lives in solitary retirement, then poverty compels him to seek employment; he claims to be an accomplished scribe and is told there is no vacancy.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"Because hunger presses, Gushtsp asks the master of the camel-drivers for service; there is no vacancy, but the master gives him a hearty meal.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"Gushtsp is accepted for work in a blacksmith’s shop; the first blow he strikes breaks the anvil to pieces, and the blacksmith angrily drives him out with reproaches.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"Gushtsp travels on, sorrowful; he meets a husbandman in a field of corn, who asks the cause of his grief, learns his circumstances, pities him, takes him home, and gives him food.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"The husbandman says he is descended from Feridun and belongs to the Kainian tribe and works at cultivating the ground; Gushtsp says he is descended from Husheng (ancestor of Feridun) and therefore of the same origin; they live together amicably for a long time.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]},{"id":"obs:15","text":"The narration states that the star of Gushtsp’s fortune begins to illuminate his path and that Heaven’s favor becomes manifest.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:11"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Lohursp","description":"A king with a reputation for just and paternal administration; father of four sons.","role_refs":["role:1","role:6"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"Kai-khosru (Khosru)","description":"A prior king whose counsel Lohursp praises; his daughter is said to be mother of two of Lohursp’s sons.","role_refs":["role:7"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"fig:3","name_or_label":"Gushtsp (Gushtasp)","description":"A son of Lohursp described as intrepid and acute; rebels, goes into exile, suffers poverty, seeks work, displays great strength, and is aided by strangers.","role_refs":["role:2","role:3"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:5","ev:6","ev:8","ev:9","ev:11"]},{"id":"fig:4","name_or_label":"Zarr","description":"Brother of Gushtsp who is sent to persuade him to return and later searches for him.","role_refs":["role:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:4","ev:5"]},{"id":"fig:5","name_or_label":"Ardshr","description":"One of Lohursp’s sons, named as Zerdusht supports these campaigns as a means to spread a new religion, and conquered rulers accept the Zendavesta; the fire-worshippers’ religion is established widely. A warrior, Gurzam, secretly hostile to Isfendiyr, slanders him to Gushtsp as plotting rebellion and imprisonment of his father. Gushtsp, distressed, sends his minister Jamsp with a letter summoning Isfendiyr. Despite foreboding and Jamsp’s counsel on obedience to a father-king, Isfendiyr comes respectfully, denies ambition, yet Gushtsp publicly treats him as a usurping son. Courtiers declare such a son should be executed or chained. Gushtsp orders Isfendiyr confined in a tower-prison on a nearby mountain, chained and bound to iron columns, where he languishes in solitude until his fortune improves.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Gushtsp crowns Isfendiyr as his successor and urges him to conquer other countries rather fire-worshippers is established in multiple lands (e.g., Rum, Hindustan, Arabia).","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Isfendiyr reports his successes by letter to content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l12098-l12188","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md","passage_locator":{"label":"LOHURSP / GUSHTSP, AND THE FAITH OF ZERDUSHT / THE HEFT-KHAN OF ISFENDIYR / CAPTURE OF THE BRAZEN FORTRESS; lines 12098-12188","start":"12098","end":"12188","translation":"Persian Literature, Volume 1","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"Isfendiyr concludes the Brazen Fortress cannot be taken by open force and decides on stratagem: he enters disguised as a merchant with a caravan, hiding warriors in chests on dromedaries and arranging a signal (a column of flame and smoke) for Bashtan to advance. Inside, Arjsp receives him and speaks derisively of Isfendiyr’s approach. Isfendiyr discovers his sisters enslaved as water-carriers; he initially denies knowing their family to avoid discovery, but they recognize his voice, secretly return at night, and he promises to restore them to liberty while urging them to continue their work at the wells until the right moment.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"After reconnoitring the fortress, Isfendiyr feels despair and believes it cannot be taken by stratagem he has imagined; a fakr reports the fort has “a hundred thousand” veteran warriors, abundant supplies, and streams of pure water.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Isfendiyr’s officers advise retreat as the safest course, but he refuses, saying victory is with God, and decides to enter the fort disguised as a merchant.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Isfendiyr puts Bashtan in temporary charge of the army and explains that stratagem, not arms, must be used to take the Brazen Fortress.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Isfendiyr assembles a caravan of one hundred dromedaries: some carry luxury goods; eighty carry two chests each with a warrior hidden inside (160 total), plus 100 more as camel-drivers/servants (260 warriors total).","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Isfendiyr tells Bashtan to march the army to the fort’s gates when he sees a column of flame and smoke rising from inside the fortress.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The caravan claims to be merchants from Persia; Arjsp permits them to enter the fortress, and Isfendiyr (using the name Kherd) delivers presents and is invited to the palace as often as he wishes.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Arjsp asks about Kurugsar and about Gushtsp and Isfendiyr; on hearing that Isfendiyr is said to be coming by the Heft-khan, Arjsp smiles and says even winged creatures fear that route and that Isfendiyr would lose a thousand lives attempting it.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Isfendiyr finds his sisters employed drawing and carrying water for Arjsp’s kitchen; they approach the caravan master for news of their father and brother, describe their servitude, and later recognize Isfendiyr by his voice.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:6","ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"At night the sisters return to speak with Isfendiyr; he acknowledges himself and says he has undertaken to restore them to liberty, telling them to continue their labor at the wells until an opportunity occurs.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Isfendiyr","description":"A hero who plans to take the Brazen Fortress by disguise as a merchant, entering with a caravan and hidden warriors, and who intends to free his sisters from servitude.","role_refs":["role:1","role:2","role:3"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:2","ev:3","ev:5","ev:6","ev:8"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"Arjsp","description":"King in control of the Brazen Fortress who permits the merchants to enter, receives gifts, and questions the disguised Isfendiyr; he holds Isfendiyr’s sisters in servitude.","role_refs":["role:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:5","ev:6"]},{"id":"fig:3","name_or_label":"Bashtan","description":"Brother of Isfendiyr placed in temporary command of the army and meet him at night.","role_refs":["role:7"],"evidence_refs":["ev:6","ev:7","ev:8"]},{"id":"fig:6","name_or_label":"Gushtsp","description":"Named as the father of the two enslaved daughters; discussed he has been put to death.","role_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:5"]}],"roles":[{"id":"role:1","label":"Disguised infiltrator (merchant persona)","assigned_to":["fig:1"],"basis":"Isfendiyr resolves to attempt infiltration by disguise.","figure_refs":["fig:1","fig:4"],"symbol_refs":["sym:5","sym:2"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:2"]},{"id":"scene:2","label":"Caravan infiltration plan and signal gates.","figure_refs":["fig:1","fig:3"],"symbol_refs":["sym:1","sym:3","sym:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:3","ev:4"]},{"id":"scene:3","label":"Entry into the fortress and court Isfendiyr, posing as Kherd, delivers gifts, gains repeated access to the palace, answers questions about events in Persia, and hears Arjsp mock the supposed approach of Isfendiyr via the Heft-khan route.","figure_refs":["fig:1","fig:2","fig:7","fig:6"],"symbol_refs":["sym:3"],"evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"scene:4","label":"Discovery of enslaved sisters and secret recognition","summary":"Isfendiyr discovers his sisters drawing and carrying water; to avoid exposure he denies knowledge of their family, but they lament their servitude. The elder sister recognizes his voice, and both keep the secret until night when they return to speak with him.","figure_refs":["fig:1","fig:5"],"symbol_refs":["sym:2"],"evidence_refs":["ev:6","ev:7"]},{"id":"scene:5","label":"Night meeting and promise of liberation","summary":"At night Isfendiyr acknowledges himself to his sisters, states his intention to free them, and instructs them to continue their work at the wells until a suitable opportunity arises.","figure_refs":["fig:1","fig:5"],"symbol_refs":["sym:2"],"evidence_refs":["ev:8"]}],"candidate_motifs":[{"id":"motif:1","label":"Hero infiltrates enemy stronghold by disguise as a merchant","taxonomy_refs":["trickster_boundary"],"basis":"Isfendiyr chooses stratagem over arms, enters the Brazen Fortress under the semblance of a peaceful merchant (name Kherd) and uses trade/gifts to gain access.","evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:5"],"confidence":"high","cautions":"Classed under a boundary-crossing/deception family; {
  "record_id": "batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l12190-l12307",
  "source_text_path": "texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md",
  "passage_locator": {
    "label": "LOHURSP / GUSHTSP, AND THE FAITH OF ZERDUSHT / THE HEFT-KHAN OF ISFENDIYR / CAPTURE OF THE BRAZEN FORTRESS; lines 12190-12307",
    "start": "12190",
    "end": "12307",
    "translation": "Persian Literature, Volume 1",
    "notes": "Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."
  },
  "canonical_text": {
    "quote": "",
    "summary": "Isfendiyr (described here as operating through a deception) invites Arjsp and his warriors to a banquet on the highest part of a fortress, where the guests become intoxicated. A large fire is lit as a signal; Bashtan attacks the fortress gates with horsemen while calling himself Isfendiyr. At night Isfendiyr releases warriors hidden in chests and, aided by his sisters, reaches Arjsp’s chamber and kills Arjsp in close combat. Arjsp’s female relatives are taken captive and placed in the custody of Isfendiyr’s son(s). After further fighting, Isfendiyr defeats and beheads Kahram. Isfendiyr proclaims pardon to those who join him and then subjugates surrounding provinces, killing those who remain hostile and appropriating Arjsp’s women and distributing daughters to his sons; the conquered realm is described as left without throne or crown and governed by a stranger.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "summarized"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "Isfendiyr tells the king he had vowed to give a splendid banquet if Heaven smiled on him again, and invites the king to attend.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "The king accepts and says he will come with all his warriors and soldiers; the feast is moved to the loftiest part of the fortress with tents/pavilions and a large fire to add splendor.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "The guests drink wine, become intoxicated, and Kherd orders the collected logs to be set on fire so that smoke and flame rise as a signal.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "Bashtan sees the sign and hastens with two thousand horsemen to the fortress gates, killing people he meets while calling himself Isfendiyr.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "Arjsp is told that Isfendiyr has entered the fort killing many, and he orders his son Kahram with fifty thousand horsemen to repel the invader, assigns additional troops to the walls, and keeps ten thousand as a personal guard.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "At night Isfendiyr opens chests and releases one hundred and sixty warriors, arms them, and also releases one hundred people disguised as camel-drivers and servants.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "Isfendiyr’s sisters arrive, identify Arjsp’s chamber, and Isfendiyr rouses Arjsp, who is described as nearly insensible from wine; Isfendiyr kills Arjsp in a violent struggle.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:8",
      "text": "Two wives, two daughters, and one sister of Arjsp are taken by the conqueror and delivered into the custody of Isfendiyr’s son to be conveyed home.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:9",
      "text": "Kahram fights Bashtan and is reduced; hearing that Arjsp has been slain, he later engages Isfendiyr and his warriors; Isfendiyr challenges Kahram to personal combat, throws him down, binds his hands, and cleaves off his head.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:10",
      "text": "After Kahram’s death, Isfendiyr issues a proclamation offering full pardon to all who will unite under his banners; the country is described as having no king, no throne, and no crown.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:11",
      "text": "Isfendiyr writes to his father about the victory, subjugates surrounding provinces, puts hostile people to death, takes Arjsp’s women into service, and gives their daughters to his sons; the conquered realm is described as desolated and stripped of treasure.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:9"]
    }
  ],
  "figures": [
    {
      "id": "fig:1",
      "name_or_label": "Isfendiyr",
      "description": "Organizer of the banquet, releaser of hidden warriors, killer of Arjsp and Kahram, issuer of pardon proclamation, and subjugator of provinces.",
      "role_refs": ["role:1", "role:2", "role:6"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:4", "ev:5", "ev:7", "ev:8", "ev:9"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:2",
      "name_or_label": "Arjsp",
      "description": "King who attends the banquet, becomes intoxicated, orders forces against the invader, fights Isfendiyr, and is killed; his female relatives are captured.",
      "role_refs": ["role:3"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3", "ev:5", "ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:3",
      "name_or_label": "Kherd",
      "description": "Associated with the banquet and orders the logs to be set on fire; later named in a report as the slayer of Arjsp.",
      "role_refs": ["role:4"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2", "ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:4",
      "name_or_label": "Bashtan",
      "description": "Sees the fire signal, attacks the fortress gates with two thousand horsemen, fights Kahram, and later comes up on Kahram’s rear during the engagement.",
      "role_refs": ["role:5"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2", "ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:5",
      "name_or_label": "Kahram",
      "description": "Son of Arjsp who leads cavalry to repel the invader, later accepts a personal combat challenge from Isfendiyr, and is killed by beheading.",
      "role_refs": ["role:7"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3", "ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:6",
      "name_or_label": "Sisters of Isfendiyr",
      "description": "Arrive and point out Arjsp’s chamber to Isfendiyr.",
      "role_refs": ["role:8"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:7",
      "name_or_label": "Son(s) of Isfendiyr",
      "description": "Receives captured women into custody for conveyance home; later receives daughters of Arjsp’s women as gifts.",
      "role_refs": ["role:9"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6", "ev:9"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:8",
      "name_or_label": "Captured female relatives of Arjsp (two wives, two daughters, one sister)",
      "description": "Taken into the hands of the conqueror and delivered into custody to be conveyed home.",
      "role_refs": ["role:10"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:9",
      "name_or_label": "Hidden warriors (160) and disguised followers (100 camel-drivers/servants)",
      "description": "Released from chests at night and armed by Isfendiyr; accompanied by those disguised as camel-drivers and servants.",
      "role_refs": ["role:11"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    }
  ],
  "roles": [
    {
      "id": "role:1",
      "label": "Deceptive host / strategist",
      "assigned_to": ["fig:1"],
      "basis": "Isfendiyr uses a stated vow and a banquet invitation as part of a plan, including arranging the feast location and coordinating a signal and infiltration.",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:2", "ev:4"]
    },

    "label": "LOHURSP / GUSHTSP, AND THE FAITH OF ZERDUSHT / THE HEFT-KHAN OF ISFENDIYR / CAPTURE OF THE BRAZEN FORTRESS; lines 12874-12966",
    "start": "12874",
    "end": "12966",
    "translation": "Persian Literature, Volume 1",
    "notes": "Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."
  },
  "canonical_text": {
    "quote": "",
    "summary": "After Bahman reports deaths and defeat, Isfendiyr accuses Rustem of treachery. Rustem swears innocence and offers to surrender relatives for punishment, but Isfendiyr insists on killing Rustem. They exchange arrows; Isfendiyr's arrows badly wound Rustem and his horse Rakush, while Rustem's arrows do not affect Isfendiyr. As night falls they agree to pause and fight again tomorrow. Isfendiyr tends the severed heads of his kinsmen and sends them to his father Gushtsp with a letter; he privately remarks that Rustem is extraordinarily tough though wounded. Rustem returns to his tent where his father Zl (Zal) treats his wounds with balm; Rustem laments Isfendiyr's seemingly brazen, invulnerable body and considers fleeing. Zal recalls the Smrgh's promise: if a feather is burned she will appear. Zal burns a feather in a censer on a high place; the Smrgh arrives and heals Rakush by pulling out arrows and passing a feather over the wounds.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "summarized"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "Bahman reports to his father that two relatives were killed by warriors of Zbul, and that Bahman's troops were routed with great slaughter.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "Isfendiyr accuses Rustem of treachery; Rustem swears innocence by the king's head and life, by the sun, and by his sword, and offers to surrender his brother Zra and his son (Fermurz is also named) for punishment.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "Isfendiyr rejects sacrificing Rustem's relatives and instead declares he will put Rustem to death; they both shoot arrows rapidly, and Isfendiyr's arrows wound Rustem and Rakush while Rustem's arrows make no impression on Isfendiyr.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "Rakush, badly wounded, runs off riderless; Zra finds Rustem desperately wounded and bleeding; Rustem notes Isfendiyr shows no bleeding.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "Isfendiyr mocks Rustem with a taunting speech comparing him to a fox and recalling his former fearsome reputation.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "Zra offers to fight Isfendiyr, but Rustem refuses; Isfendiyr demands Rustem consent to be fettered; Rustem proposes to resume the fight tomorrow; Isfendiyr agrees and they separate at nightfall.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "Isfendiyr embraces the severed heads of his kinsmen, places them on a bier, and sends them to his father Gushtsp with a letter about obeying commands and uncertainty about tomorrow.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:8",
      "text": "Isfendiyr tells Bashtan privately that Rustem is 'not human' and like 'rock and iron'; he notes arrows went deep and wonders if Rustem will survive the night.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:9",
      "text": "Zl (Zal) sees Rustem's wounds, laments, rubs Rustem's feet, applies healing balm, and binds the wounds like a physician.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:9"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:10",
      "text": "Rustem says Isfendiyr seems to have a 'brazen body' that Rustem's arrows cannot penetrate; Rustem thanks God for night and expresses a wish to retire unseen from the struggle.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:10"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:11",
      "text": "Zl recalls the Smrgh's promise that burning one of her feathers will cause her to appear; Zl burns a feather in a censer on a high place and the Smrgh appears.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:11"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:12",
      "text": "The Smrgh heals Rakush by plucking out embedded arrows with her beak and passing a feather over the wounds so they heal quickly.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:12"]
    }
  ],

Rustem asks for help against Isfendiyr; the Smrgh praises Isfendiyr as an unmatched hero favored by Heaven and warns Rustem to keep away. Zal argues that retreat would enslave their family. The Smrgh leads Rustem across a great river to reed-covered ground where the Kaz-tree grows, rubs a feather on Rustem’s eyes, and instructs him to make a forked arrow from a Kaz-tree branch straightened in fire and to shoot Isfendiyr in the eyes, blinding him. The Smrgh warns that whoever spills Isfendiyr’s blood will suffer lifelong calamity and states that Kaz-tree arrows never miss. Rustem prepares the arrow and, at dawn, finds Isfendiyr sleeping and challenges him. Isfendiyr sends Bashtan to check Rustem’s condition and horse. Rustem boasts he and Rakush are unwounded and claims to possess an elixir that instantly heals. Bashtan reports Rustem looks vigorous and recommends reconciliation.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The Smrgh draws out arrows from Rustem’s wounds, sucks blood from them, and the wounds close; Rustem is restored to life and power.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The Smrgh says she cannot assist Rustem further and states that no hero as brave and perfect as Isfendiyr has appeared; she says Heaven’s favor is with Isfendiyr and advises Rustem that distance from Isfendiyr’s arm increases safety.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Zal says that if Rustem retires, Rustem’s family will be enslaved and Zal will share their bondage and affliction.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Rustem mounts Rakush and follows the Smrgh; they cross a great river and arrive at a reed-covered place where the Kaz-tree abounds.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The Smrgh rubs a feather on Rustem’s eyes and instructs him to take a branch of the Kaz-tree, straighten it upon fire, and form it into a forked arrow.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The Smrgh instructs Rustem to shoot the arrow into Isfendiyr’s eyes; throne.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"A bier arrives in Persia at Gushtsp’s palace, and there is widespread public and domestic Rustem and his horse Rakush fall into multiple pits, escaping repeatedly until both are exhausted and grievously wounded. Rustem confronts Shughad about the treachery; Shughad claims the death is divine vengeance for Rustem’s bloodshed. The king feigns pity and offers medicine, which Rustem rejects, predicting that Fermurz will avenge him.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Astrologers predict at Shughad’s birth that he will be the ruin of the house of Sam and Narmn and {
  "record_id": "batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l13335-l13446",
  "source_text_path": "texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md",
  "passage_locator": {
    "label": "CAPTURE OF THE BRAZEN FORTRESS / THE DEATH OF ISFENDIYR / THE DEATH OF RUSTEM / BAHMAN; lines 13335-13446",
    "start": "13335",
    "end": "13446",
    "translation": "Persian Literature, Volume 1",
    "notes": "Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."
  },
  "canonical_text": {
    "quote": "",
    "summary": "Bahman, grandson of Gushtsp, seeks vengeance on Rustem’s family for Isfendiyr’s death, invades Sistan, negotiates with and then humiliates and plunders the aged Zal, imprisons him, fights Zal’s son Fermurz (whose defeat is aided by a hurricane), captures and hangs Fermurz, is dissuaded by Bashtan from massacring Sistan’s people, frees Zal and restores Sistan, later dies from a snakebite, and leaves succession to his wife Hma with a conditional heir arrangement.",
    "language": "English",
    "quote_policy": "summarized"
  },
  "literal_observations": [
    {
      "id": "obs:1",
      "text": "Bahman states he will take revenge on Rustem’s family for the death of Isfendiyr and cites ancestral precedent for vengeance.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:2",
      "text": "A force of one hundred thousand veteran troops is assembled to invade Sistan, and Bahman advances to the borders of the river Behermund.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:3",
      "text": "Bahman sends a message to Zal declaring his purpose and demanding the sacrifice of Zal and his family as atonement for Rustem’s guilt.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:2"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:4",
      "text": "Zal replies that Rustem was not at fault, recounting Rustem’s reluctance to be bound and offering wealth; Zal offers his house and treasure but asks that his family and himself be spared.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:3"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:5",
      "text": "Bahman’s heart is softened enough that Zal is not to suffer; Zal meets Bahman with presents and prostrates himself; Zal chooses to go barefoot in homage as his ancestor Sm did.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:4"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:6",
      "text": "Bahman enters Zal’s abode in an unappeased spirit, confiscates goods, plunders rooms, and seizes treasure for his own use.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:5"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:7",
      "text": "Zal claims Fermurz has gone hunting, but Bahman sees through this and puts Zal in fetters.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:6"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:8",
      "text": "Fermurz has secretly withdrawn with the Zabul army, then marches against Bahman when he learns Zal is confined; the armies fight for three days and nights.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:9",
      "text": "On the fourth day a hurricane blows dust into the Zabul army’s faces, blinding and impeding them while the enemy are driven forward by wind at their backs, resulting in Zabul’s defeat.",
      "category": "setting",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:8"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:10",
      "text": "A verse passage states that death by sword or arrow is not given unless decreed by Heaven, and the narrative says it was decreed that Fermurz’s exertions would be unsuccessful.",
      "category": "attribute",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:9"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:11",
      "text": "Fermurz’s horse falls; he is severely wounded; while insensible he is secured, conveyed in fetters to Bahman, and Bahman orders him to be hanged.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:10"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:12",
      "text": "Bahman orders the people of Sistan to be put to the sword; Bashtan protests on behalf of innocent people, urges fear of God, and asks for mercy; Bahman is withdrawn from the purpose, liberates Zal, restores Sistan to him, and returns to Persia.",
      "category": "sequence",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:11"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:13",
      "text": "Bahman later is bitten by a snake, cannot be cured, and dies from the wound in the eighth year of his reign.",
      "category": "action",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:12"]
    },
    {
      "id": "obs:14",
      "text": "Although Bahman has a son named Sassn, he does not appoint him; he gives crown and throne to his wife Hma, stating that if she has a son he shall succeed, but if a daughter Hma shall continue to reign.",
      "category": "speech",
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:13"]
    }
  ],
  "figures": [
    {
      "id": "fig:1",
      "name_or_label": "Bahman",
      "description": "King and grandson of Gushtsp; invades Sistan, takes vengeance on Rustem’s family, later dies from a snakebite, and assigns succession to his wife Hma.",
      "role_refs": ["role:1", "role:8"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1", "ev:12", "ev:13"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:2",
      "name_or_label": "Gushtsp",

      "role_refs": ["role:2", "role:6"],

    },
    {

      "name_or_label": "Rustem",

    },

      "role_refs": ["role:10"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:6",
      "name_or_label": "Fermurz",

      "role_refs": ["role:3", "role:7"],
      "evidence_refs": ["ev:7", "ev:10", "ev:11"]
    },
    {
      "id": "fig:7",

    },

      "evidence_refs": ["ev:1"]
    }
  ],

{
  "record_id": "batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l13449-l13550",

    "label": "THE DEATH OF ISFENDIYR / THE DEATH OF RUSTEM / BAHMAN / HMAI AND THE BIRTH OF DRB; lines 13449-13550",
